articles.title: AWS IAM fundamentals: root user, users, groups, roles and policies
articles.scope: Explains that IAM is an authorization system scoped to each account, not a directory. Covers the root user (full access in its account unless SCPs or RCPs limit it in a member account; centralized root access can remove member-account root credentials altogether) and the tasks only root can do, IAM users vs groups vs roles, long-term vs temporary credentials, access keys, MFA and password policies, and ARNs. Introduces the ways to reach AWS (console, CLI, SDKs, raw APIs and IaC), all of which sign requests with SigV4, and links cloud/aws/iac-devops for the SDK credential chain and cloud/foundations for the neutral management-interfaces page. Contrasts it with Entra ID (tenant directory) plus Azure RBAC, so the reader can say why AWS pushes humans to federation and workloads to roles.

articles.title: IAM policy types compared: identity-based, resource-based, permissions boundaries, session policies, SCPs, RCPs and ACLs
articles.scope: Sets out each policy type by where it attaches, whether it can grant or only limit, and which principals it affects. Covers AWS managed vs customer managed vs inline policies and which services support resource-based policies. Ends with a decision table for which lever to use in a given situation.

articles.title: How AWS evaluates a request: policy evaluation logic within and across accounts
articles.scope: Walks the evaluation flow documented on the IAM 'policy-eval-denyallow' page (rewritten 30 Jan 2025): an explicit deny anywhere wins; RCPs, SCPs, permissions boundaries and session policies act as ceilings that must all allow; within one account an allow in EITHER an identity-based or a resource-based policy is enough. Shows why the principal matters: a resource-policy grant to an IAM user ARN or a role session ARN is not limited by implicit denies in boundaries or session policies, while a grant to a role ARN is. Covers the exceptions that need an explicit allow on the resource side (role trust policies, KMS key policies), RCPFullAWSAccess being auto-attached when RCPs are enabled, and why cross-account requests need an allow on both sides. Ends with a worked AccessDenied decoder, so the reader can predict any allow or deny result. KMS key-policy depth links to cloud/aws/security-services.

articles.title: IAM policy language reference: elements, operators, policy variables and condition keys
articles.scope: Reference for Effect, Action/NotAction, Resource/NotResource, Principal/NotPrincipal and Condition, the condition operators, IfExists, ForAllValues/ForAnyValue and policy variables. Explains condition context keys: global keys (aws:*) vs service-specific keys (such as s3:prefix or iam:PassedToService). Includes a curated table of keys: aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:PrincipalOrgPaths, aws:PrincipalArn, aws:ResourceOrgID, aws:SourceVpce, aws:VpceAccount/aws:VpceOrgID/aws:VpceOrgPaths, aws:RequestedRegion, aws:PrincipalTag, aws:SecureTransport, aws:CalledVia, aws:ViaAWSService, and the cross-service confused-deputy keys aws:SourceArn, aws:SourceAccount, aws:SourceOrgID, aws:SourceOrgPaths and aws:PrincipalIsAWSService, plus iam:ServiceSpecificCredentialAgeDays and iam:ServiceSpecificCredentialServiceName (Sep 2025). Snippets are given in JSON, CDK (C#/Python) and Terraform.

articles.title: AWS STS and role assumption: trust policies, cross-account access, role chaining and federation APIs
articles.scope: Contrasts trust policies with permissions policies, and role ARNs (arn:aws:iam::...:role/...) with role session ARNs (arn:aws:sts::...:assumed-role/...), because policy evaluation treats them differently. Covers AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithSAML, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, GetSessionToken, GetFederationToken and AssumeRoot (task-scoped root sessions in member accounts, Nov 2024); session duration and the one-hour role-chaining limit; the external ID against the cross-account confused deputy; source identity and session tags with the sts:SetSourceIdentity and sts:TagSession permissions they require; regional vs global STS endpoints, global-endpoint v1 vs v2 session tokens, and the fact that GetWebIdentityToken is not available on the global endpoint. Compares cross-account access via role assumption, resource-based policies and AWS RAM, with C# and Python SDK samples.

articles.title: Workload credentials on AWS: instance profiles, execution roles, IAM Roles Anywhere, OIDC federation and outbound identity federation
articles.scope: Compares the ways workloads get temporary credentials: EC2 instance profiles, Lambda execution roles, ECS task roles vs task execution roles, EKS (linked to the containers section), IAM Roles Anywhere for on-premises machines, and OIDC federation for CI such as GitHub Actions. Covers the mandatory claim checks for shared OIDC providers (enforced 6 Jun 2025; Cognito, Azure Sentinel, Pulumi and Vercel added Aug 2025) and IAM accepting either the sub claim or job_workflow_ref for GitHub (12 May 2026), plus STS GetWebIdentityToken for AWS-to-external calls. Shows cross-cloud federation in both directions (Entra workload identity to AWS, AWS JWT to Azure). Builds on security/workload-identity without duplicating it, and links ai/platforms for AgentCore Identity (an unscored SAP-C02 Emerging Topic).

articles.title: Human access to AWS: IAM users vs IAM SAML/OIDC federation vs IAM Identity Center vs AWS Directory Service
articles.scope: Decision guide for workforce access. Compares IAM users, direct IAM identity-provider federation, IAM Identity Center with an external IdP such as Entra ID, and the directory options: AWS Managed Microsoft AD, AD Connector and Simple AD. Explains when to federate a directory with IAM roles and how each option fits multi-account estates and Windows workloads.

articles.title: IAM Identity Center: permission sets, account assignments, identity sources and multi-Region
articles.scope: Explains organization vs account instances, the three identity source types (Identity Center directory, Active Directory, external IdP with SAML 2.0 and SCIM), permission sets and account assignments, and the access portal and CLI sign-in. Also covers ABAC attributes, delegated administration, trusted identity propagation, identity-enhanced console sessions and user background sessions. Tracks the 2025-2026 changes: customer managed KMS keys (17 Sep 2025); AD Sync deprecated in favour of configurable AD sync (Apr 2025); multi-Region support (2 Feb 2026) extended to the Identity Center directory (28 Jul 2026) and one-click multi-Region creation (6 Aug 2026); opt-in Regions, GovCloud and China (30 Sep 2026); multi-account permissions optional for new instances (4 Aug 2026); and separate 7,000 quotas for accounts and for applications (Jun 2026). Maps each construct to Entra ID groups, Azure RBAC role assignments and PIM, with fidelity ratings.

articles.title: ABAC on AWS: principal tags, resource tags, session tags and scaling permissions
articles.scope: Shows how to scale authorization with aws:PrincipalTag, aws:ResourceTag, aws:RequestTag and aws:TagKeys conditions. Covers session tags passed from an IdP, transitive tags, Identity Center attributes for access control, tag governance with tag policies, and services that do not support tag-based conditions. Weighs ABAC against RBAC and links to security/iam for the neutral concept.

articles.title: Permissions boundaries: safely delegating IAM administration without privilege escalation
articles.scope: Explains the intersection semantics of boundaries and the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition that forces delegated admins to attach one. Covers blocking escalation paths (iam:PassRole, policy versioning) and how boundaries differ from SCPs and session policies. Contrasts with Azure's constrained role-assignment delegation (ABAC conditions) as a partial equivalent.

articles.title: Least privilege and access troubleshooting: IAM Access Analyzer, policy simulator, last-accessed data and AccessDenied messages
articles.scope: Uses external, internal and unused access analyzers, policy validation, custom policy checks in CI, and policy generation from CloudTrail activity. Covers the credential report and the policy simulator, plus decoding AccessDenied messages that name the blocking policy type. The reader leaves with a repeatable least-privilege review and triage process.

articles.title: Amazon Cognito: user pools vs identity pools for customer and app identity
articles.scope: Contrasts user pools (an OIDC user directory with managed login, MFA and federation) with identity pools (which exchange tokens for temporary AWS credentials). Covers feature plans, token types, and integration with ALB, API Gateway and Amazon Verified Permissions. Rates the mapping to Entra External ID and shows token validation in ASP.NET Core and Python.

articles.title: AWS multi-account strategy: accounts as isolation boundaries and recommended OU structures
articles.scope: Explains why the account is AWS's hard boundary for blast radius, quotas and billing, and walks through the recommended OUs (Security, Infrastructure, Workloads, Sandbox, Policy Staging, Suspended, Exceptions). Covers account vending and when to split accounts. Maps the AWS model to Azure tenants, management groups, subscriptions and resource groups, with an honest note on where subscription-as-boundary differs.

articles.title: AWS Organizations and AWS RAM: management account, OUs, consolidated billing, trusted access, delegated administrators and resource sharing
articles.scope: Opens with a CLF-depth section (organization root, management and member accounts, consolidated billing and RI/Savings Plans sharing), then goes to practitioner depth: all-features vs consolidated-billing-only mode, trusted access, delegated administrators, and account migration and closure. Explains AWS RAM sharing of subnets, transit gateways, Resolver rules, prefix lists and Capacity Reservations, including the organization-only option. Includes CDK and Terraform for building an OU tree.

articles.title: Organization policies compared: SCPs vs RCPs vs declarative policies (EC2, tag, backup, AI opt-out and more)
articles.scope: Contrasts principal ceilings (SCPs), resource ceilings (RCPs) and control-plane configuration enforcement (declarative policies). Lists the declarative types as documented: Amazon EC2, Backup, Tag, Chat applications, AI services opt-out, Security Hub, Amazon Inspector, Amazon Bedrock, Upgrade rollout, Amazon S3, AWS Shield network security director and Amazon GuardDuty; VPC Block Public Access, VPC Encryption Controls and Allowed AMIs are attributes inside Amazon EC2 policies, not types. Explains that declarative policies also affect the management account, govern service-linked roles and roll back on detach, while SCPs and RCPs do not touch the management account. Covers RCP exclusions (service-linked roles, AWS managed KMS keys, kms:RetireGrant, management-account resources; delegated-admin accounts are included), inheritance and effective policies, and limits: SCPs 10 per target and 10,240 characters, RCPs 5 and 5,120, declarative 10 and 10,000. Compares each with Azure Policy effects and deny assignments.

articles.title: Organization guardrails and security baseline: SCP patterns, centralized root access, delegated admins and break-glass
articles.scope: Catalogs proven guardrails: deny leaving the organization, Region deny with exemptions, protecting baseline roles and trails, and denying root usage. Covers centralized root access management for member accounts, MFA and break-glass design, delegated admin placement for security services, an organization trail, and a Config aggregator. Also covers safe guardrail rollout with a Policy Staging OU.

articles.title: Data perimeters on AWS: identity, resource and network perimeters with SCPs, RCPs and VPC endpoint policies
articles.scope: Builds the three perimeters: trusted identities, trusted resources and expected networks. Uses aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:ResourceOrgID, aws:SourceVpce, the 2025 aws:VpceOrgID family, RCPs and endpoint policies, with service-principal exceptions handled correctly. Links to security/cloud-security for the neutral zero-trust framing and rates the mapping to Azure Private Link, network security perimeter and Azure Policy.

articles.title: AWS Control Tower and landing zones: controls, Account Factory, AFT, drift and landing zone 4.0
articles.scope: Explains the landing zone, the control behaviors (preventive, detective, proactive) and guidance levels (mandatory, strongly recommended, elective), the Control Catalog (renamed from Controls Library, Jun 2025), drift and its remediation, and Account Factory vs AFT (plan-only runs, Sep 2026) vs CfCT. Covers landing zone 4.0 (17 Nov 2025) precisely: optional integrations for Config, CloudTrail, Security Roles and AWS Backup (disabling Config also requires disabling Security Roles, IAM Identity Center and Backup); no Security OU required, with hub accounts in one OU; a dedicated controls experience without AWSControlTowerBaseline; a service-linked Config aggregator replacing org and account aggregators; service-linked Config rules (Jun 2025); and per-service SNS topics. Notes availability in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (13 Jan 2026) and Landing Zone Accelerator as an alternative. Compares with Azure Landing Zones (partial).

articles.title: AWS Config: recording, rules, conformance packs, aggregators and automatic remediation
articles.scope: Covers the configuration recorder and recording modes, configuration items and history, service-linked recorders, managed vs custom (Lambda and Guard) rules, proactive evaluation, and conformance packs including the 2026 AI/ML packs. Also covers organization aggregators, advanced queries and remediation through Systems Manager Automation. Compares with Azure Policy compliance and Resource Graph change analysis.

articles.title: AWS CloudTrail for governance: event types, organization trails, log integrity and centralized audit
articles.scope: Covers management, data, network activity and Insights events; trails vs event data stores; organization and multi-Region trails; and log file integrity validation and SSE-KMS. Explains centralized delivery to a Log Archive account and event enrichment. CloudTrail Lake closed to new customers on 2026-05-31, so the page gives the forward path for new estates (organization trail to S3 queried with Athena, CloudWatch Logs Insights on a trail delivered to CloudWatch Logs, and Amazon Security Lake) and keeps Lake content for existing customers. Compares with the Azure Activity Log and resource logs.

articles.title: Governance and audit services compared: Organizations policies vs Control Tower vs Config vs CloudTrail vs CloudWatch vs Trusted Advisor
articles.scope: Sorts each service into prevent, detect, record, observe or advise, answering 'what changed', 'who did it', 'is it compliant' and 'how is it behaving'. Adds Audit Manager and Artifact as pointers into the security-services section. Settles the classic CLF and associate-exam confusion with one matrix and an Azure column.

articles.title: AWS tagging strategy: tag policies, cost allocation tags, ABAC tags and enforcement
articles.scope: Designs a tag taxonomy (cost center, owner, environment, data classification) and enforces it with tag policies, SCP tag conditions, Config rules and IaC defaults. Shows how a data-classification tag scheme drives handling controls (backup, encryption, Macie scope), the CloudOps 4.2.1 skill. Covers activating user-defined and AWS-generated cost allocation tags, Tag Editor, Resource Groups and Resource Explorer. Links to cloud/aws/cost for the reporting side and compares with Azure tags (case-insensitive names) and tag inheritance.

articles.title: Service Quotas and Trusted Advisor: managing limits, throttling and best-practice checks across accounts
articles.scope: Covers applied vs default quotas, account-level vs resource-level quotas, increase requests, quota request templates, Service Quotas Automatic Management, and CloudWatch usage alarms, including pre-raising quotas in DR Regions. Explains Trusted Advisor categories, check availability by support plan (full checks need a Business-tier or higher plan: Business Support+, Enterprise or Unified Operations, or legacy Business and Enterprise On-Ramp until their retirement), the organizational view, Priority and EventBridge automation. Support plans themselves are in aws-support-plans-and-aws-health.

articles.title: Central logging and multi-account event notifications: organization trail, Config aggregator, EventBridge cross-account and cross-Region buses, AWS Health organizational view and AWS User Notifications
articles.scope: Designs the security and operations event backbone for an organization: an organization trail to a Log Archive account, the Config aggregator, EventBridge rules forwarding to a central bus across accounts and Regions, the AWS Health organizational view and Health events, AWS User Notifications, and Security Hub cross-Region aggregation (depth in cloud/aws/security-services). Covers delegated-admin placement, alert routing to chat and ticketing, automated incident reporting, and what each source cannot tell you. CloudWatch cross-account observability links to cloud/aws/observability. Maps to Azure Monitor diagnostic settings via Azure Policy, Activity Log alerts and Service Health (partial).

articles.title: AWS Support plans, AWS Health and customer enablement: Basic vs Business Support+ vs Enterprise vs Unified Operations, Health Dashboard and Health API, Trust & Safety, re:Post, Partners and Marketplace
articles.scope: Explains the current support portfolio (Basic, Business Support+, Enterprise, Unified Operations) and the transition from the legacy plans: Developer and Business closed to new subscriptions on 2 Dec 2025 and remain available until 1 Jan 2027; the Enterprise On-Ramp path is hedged until AWS documents it. Shows what each plan unlocks (response times, Trusted Advisor checks, Shield Response Team access, TAMs). Covers the AWS Health Dashboard (service vs account health), the Health API and organizational view, AWS Trust & Safety for abuse reports, AWS re:Post and Knowledge Center, AWS Partners and AWS Marketplace. Maps to Azure support plans, Service Health and Resource Health (close).

articles.title: AWS Service Catalog and governed self-service: portfolios, products, constraints, AppRegistry and how Account Factory builds on it
articles.scope: Explains portfolios shared across accounts and the organization, products backed by CloudFormation or Terraform, versions, and launch, template, tag-update, notification and StackSet constraints that let users provision without broad IAM rights. Covers AppRegistry applications and attribute groups, and shows how Control Tower Account Factory is a Service Catalog product. Compares with Azure template specs and managed applications service catalog (partial), with CDK and Terraform examples.

articles.title: Amazon VPC fundamentals: CIDRs, AZ-scoped subnets, route tables, gateways and the VPC router
articles.scope: Explains VPC and subnet scope (regional VPC, AZ-bound subnets), the five reserved addresses, route tables and the local route, public vs private vs isolated subnets, ENIs, Elastic IPs, DHCP option sets and DNS attributes. Contrasts with Azure VNets, whose subnets span zones, and includes CloudFormation, CDK and Terraform for a three-tier VPC.

articles.title: VPC IP addressing: IPv4 planning, secondary CIDRs, IPv6 and dual-stack, BYOIP, public IPv4 charges and VPC IPAM
articles.scope: Covers CIDR planning to avoid overlap and exhaustion, secondary CIDRs and Network Address Usage metrics, IPv6-only and dual-stack subnets, NAT64/DNS64, and egress-only internet gateways. Explains BYOIP, the cost of public IPv4 addresses, managed prefix lists, and IPAM pools, scopes, tiers and policies across an organization. Includes subnet sizing for growth (CloudOps 3.1.3) and links overlapping-ip-address-space-on-aws for designs that cannot avoid overlap.

articles.title: Security groups vs network ACLs: stateful vs stateless filtering in a VPC
articles.scope: Opens with the foundation contrast: stateful, allow-only, ENI-level security groups vs stateless, ordered, subnet-level NACLs, ephemeral ports and common misconfigurations. Then goes to practitioner depth: security group referencing (including across peering, Transit Gateway and Cloud WAN), shared security groups and multi-VPC associations (30 Oct 2024), and connection tracking: tracked, untracked and automatically tracked connections, configurable idle timeouts, and the Nitro v6 default TCP established idle timeout of 350 s (down from 432,000 s), which breaks long-lived idle connections through appliances. Rates the mapping to Azure NSGs and ASGs as partial.

articles.title: Internet ingress and egress: internet gateway vs NAT gateway (zonal and regional) vs NAT instance vs egress-only IGW, plus VPC Block Public Access
articles.scope: Compares the egress options on availability, cost and operations, including one zonal NAT gateway per AZ vs a shared one, and the regional NAT gateway (Nov 2025), which expands across AZs automatically, needs no public subnet, allows up to 32 IPs per AZ (vs 8), can take up to 60 minutes to expand into a new AZ (processing cross-zone meanwhile), uses IPAM policies for your own IPs, does not support private NAT and is not available in constrained AZs. Covers private NAT gateways, ingress routing and VPC Block Public Access enforced through Amazon EC2 policies. Maps to Azure NAT Gateway and default outbound access retirement.

articles.title: VPC endpoints: gateway endpoints vs interface endpoints (PrivateLink), private DNS and endpoint policies
articles.scope: Contrasts free, route-table-based gateway endpoints (S3, DynamoDB) with per-AZ, ENI-based, billable interface endpoints. Covers private DNS, endpoint policies, access from on-premises, and centralized endpoints shared through Route 53 Profiles. Maps to Azure service endpoints (close to gateway endpoints) and private endpoints (close to interface endpoints). Distinguishes VPC endpoints from AWS service endpoints (regional, global, FIPS and dual-stack hostnames), and links cloud/aws/serverless-integration for API Gateway private APIs.

articles.title: Publishing private services: PrivateLink endpoint services vs VPC Lattice service networks and resource configurations
articles.scope: Covers the provider side of PrivateLink (NLB- or GWLB-backed endpoint services, acceptance, cross-Region access, a fix for overlapping CIDRs) and VPC Lattice (service networks, HTTP/gRPC/TLS services, auth policies, resource gateways and resource configurations for TCP resources, service-network endpoints). Adds a service-to-service section contrasting Lattice with ECS Service Connect, AWS Cloud Map, AWS App Mesh (support ended 30 Sep 2026; migrate to Service Connect) and API Gateway private APIs with VPC links, linking cloud/aws/containers and cloud/aws/serverless-integration. Shows when each fits SaaS, microservice and multi-account patterns, and maps to Azure Private Link Service (close) and to Lattice, which has no direct Azure equivalent.

articles.title: Connecting VPCs: VPC peering vs Transit Gateway vs Cloud WAN vs PrivateLink vs VPC Lattice vs VPC sharing
articles.scope: Builds a decision matrix on transitivity, CIDR overlap, scale, bandwidth, cost, cross-Region and cross-account support, and operational model. Explains why peering is non-transitive and when a proxy or service-level pattern beats network-level routing. Maps to Azure VNet peering, Virtual WAN and Private Link.

articles.title: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN: regional hubs vs policy-driven global networks
articles.scope: Covers Transit Gateway attachments (VPC, VPN, Direct Connect gateway, Connect/GRE for SD-WAN, peering, Client VPN (Apr 2026), and the network function attachment that connects a transit gateway directly to AWS Network Firewall without an inspection VPC (16 Jun 2025)), route tables, association vs propagation, blackhole routes, appliance mode and multicast domains. Covers policy tables for peering (2022) vs policy-based routing (GA 28 Jul 2026), 1:1 NAT for transit gateways for overlapping CIDRs (22 Oct 2026), Flexible Cost Allocation and Encryption Support, and the legacy transit VPC pattern Transit Gateway replaced. Contrasts with Cloud WAN's core network policy, segments, core network edges and service insertion, and with Network Manager as the shared visibility layer. Compares both with Azure Virtual WAN.

articles.title: Multi-account network patterns: VPC sharing, centralized egress, centralized inspection and shared endpoints
articles.scope: Gives reference architectures for a network account owning shared VPCs via RAM, hub-and-spoke with centralized NAT egress, inspection VPCs using Network Firewall or GWLB with appliance mode, centralized interface endpoints with Route 53 Profiles, and east-west vs north-south inspection. Explains trade-offs in cost, blast radius and team autonomy, and maps to Azure hub-spoke and Virtual WAN secured hubs.

articles.title: Hybrid and multicloud connectivity: Site-to-Site VPN vs Direct Connect vs both, SD-WAN, and AWS Interconnect - multicloud
articles.scope: Compares connectivity on bandwidth, latency, encryption, SLA, lead time and cost, including VPN as Direct Connect backup, private IP VPN over Direct Connect, Transit Gateway Connect for SD-WAN, and AWS Interconnect - multicloud (status hedged: the product page showed Azure in preview and OCI planned when checked; Google Cloud general availability is not confirmed from a primary source). Maps to ExpressRoute and Azure VPN Gateway.

articles.title: AWS Direct Connect and BGP deep dive: connections, LAGs, VIFs, Direct Connect gateway, MACsec, resiliency models and route control
articles.scope: Covers dedicated vs hosted connections (one VIF per hosted connection; up to 4 transit VIFs per dedicated connection), port speeds up to 400 Gbps (400GBASE-LR4), LOA-CFA and colocation, LAGs, private, public and transit VIFs, Direct Connect gateway (up to 6 transit gateways and 20 VGWs) and SiteLink, MACsec, and the resiliency toolkit models (maximum, high, development and test). Explains BGP control: ASNs, the 7224:7100/7200/7300 local-preference and 7224:9100/9200/9300 scope communities, NO_EXPORT, AS_PATH prepending, longest-prefix match and AWS route priority across Direct Connect, VPN and static routes; route limits (100 per BGP session by default, up to 1,000 with prefix controls; 1,000 on public VIFs) and allowed prefixes on gateway associations. Covers up to 10 rate limiters per dedicated connection and MTU and jumbo frames; flat-rate pricing and BGP route visibility are hedged until a primary source is cited.

articles.title: AWS VPN and remote access: Site-to-Site VPN, Accelerated VPN, large-bandwidth tunnels, VPN Concentrator, Client VPN and Verified Access
articles.scope: Covers the customer gateway, virtual private gateway vs Transit Gateway termination, two-tunnel design, static vs BGP routing, Accelerated VPN, 5 Gbps large-bandwidth tunnels, VPN Concentrator, CloudHub, and pre-shared keys in Secrets Manager. Compares Client VPN with Verified Access for zero-trust user access, including non-HTTP protocols. Maps to Azure VPN Gateway (S2S/P2S) and Entra Private Access.

articles.title: Amazon Route 53: hosted zones, alias records, routing policies, health checks and DNS resilience
articles.scope: Covers public vs private hosted zones, record types (including HTTPS, SVCB, TLSA and SSHFP, Oct 2024) and alias vs CNAME (including alias records to VPC Lattice domains, Jun 2025), and every routing policy (simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, IP-based, multivalue) with a comparison table, plus Traffic Flow traffic policies for versioned, nested routing trees. Also covers health checks (endpoint, calculated, CloudWatch alarm), public DNS query logging, DNSSEC signing, domain registration, accelerated recovery and ARC zonal shift. Links cloud/foundations for the DNS protocol itself. Maps to Azure DNS plus Traffic Manager (partial).

articles.title: Hybrid and multi-account DNS: Route 53 VPC Resolver endpoints, forwarding rules, Profiles, DNS Firewall and Global Resolver
articles.scope: Explains the VPC+2 resolver, DHCP options sets, inbound and outbound Resolver endpoints (DoH since Dec 2023, with SNI since Oct 2024; detailed endpoint metrics, Dec 2025), forwarding, system and delegation rules shared via RAM, private hosted zone association across accounts and split-horizon DNS. Covers Route 53 Profiles, Resolver query logging (contrasted with public DNS query logging), DNS Firewall including Advanced, DNSSEC validation, and Route 53 Global Resolver (the VPC Resolver rename is confirmed; the GA date is hedged until sourced). Maps to Azure DNS Private Resolver and private DNS zones.

articles.title: Elastic Load Balancing: ALB vs NLB vs GWLB, with target groups, cross-zone, stickiness, TLS termination vs passthrough, mTLS and JWT validation
articles.scope: Compares layer 7, layer 4 and layer 3 load balancers by listeners and rules, target types (instance, IP, Lambda, ALB-as-target), health checks, routing algorithms (round robin, least outstanding requests, weighted random with Automatic Target Weights, NLB flow hash), cross-zone behavior, zonal DNS affinity, sticky sessions, deregistration delay and proxy protocol v2. Covers scaling factors (LCUs) and capacity unit reservation, TLS policies, mTLS, ALB JWT access-token validation and transforms (2025), NLB QUIC, NLB listener rules (10 Jul 2026; route by source IP address type, so IPv4 and IPv6 can go to different target groups), weighted target groups as a default action (Nov 2025), secondary IPv4 addresses (Jul 2025), security groups, zonal shift for more target-group setups (Sep 2026), and the AWS Load Balancer Controller (depth in cloud/aws/containers). Maps to Application Gateway, Azure Load Balancer and Gateway Load Balancer.

articles.title: Edge networking: Amazon CloudFront in depth, and how it differs from AWS Global Accelerator
articles.scope: Covers CloudFront distributions, origins and origin groups, cache behaviors and cache, origin-request and response-header policies, OAC, VPC origins, signed URLs vs signed cookies, CloudFront Functions vs Lambda@Edge vs Connection Functions (viewer mTLS, Nov 2025), Origin Shield, viewer mTLS and connection logs, gRPC, standard logging v2, multi-tenant distributions and flat-rate plans. Contrasts with Global Accelerator (standard vs custom routing, client IP preservation, non-HTTP and failover use cases), and rewrites the old 'static IPs mean Global Accelerator' heuristic now that CloudFront offers Anycast static IPs (Nov 2024; dual-stack and BYOIP through IPAM, Nov 2025). Links troubleshooting-cloudfront-caching for operations. Maps to Azure Front Door and the cross-region load balancer.

articles.title: Network protection services compared: AWS WAF vs Shield vs Network Firewall vs Route 53 DNS Firewall vs Firewall Manager vs security groups
articles.scope: Maps each control to the OSI layer, traffic direction and attachment point it acts on. Covers WAF protection packs (web ACLs), managed rules, Bot Control (including Web Bot Auth and AI traffic analysis) and rate-based rules; Shield Standard vs Advanced, with the documented change that from 26 Mar 2026 the AWS WAF Anti-DDoS managed rule group is the default HTTP-flood protection and supersedes Shield Advanced Layer 7 Auto Mitigation (existing customers may keep L7AM; new customers must ask Support); Network Firewall stateless and Suricata-compatible stateful engines (strict vs default rule order), TLS inspection and the proxy preview; DNS Firewall; Shield network security director (preview); and Firewall Manager organization policies. Rates mappings to Azure WAF, DDoS Protection and Azure Firewall.

articles.title: Encryption in transit across AWS networks: Nitro encryption, VPC Encryption Controls, MACsec, IPsec and TLS termination points
articles.scope: Explains which paths AWS encrypts automatically (Nitro instance-to-instance traffic, inter-Region backbone) and VPC Encryption Controls' monitor and enforce modes, Transit Gateway Encryption Support and declarative controls. Covers MACsec on Direct Connect, VPN over Direct Connect, and TLS termination vs passthrough at CloudFront and ELB, using ACM and Private CA. Places each in the shared responsibility model.

articles.title: Troubleshooting AWS networks: VPC Flow Logs, Reachability Analyzer, Network Access Analyzer, Traffic Mirroring, MTU and common failure patterns
articles.scope: A systematic triage path through route tables, security groups, NACLs, connection tracking, NAT, endpoints, DNS and MTU/PMTUD inside a VPC. Covers flow log default and custom fields (including Transit Gateway flow logs), Reachability Analyzer intent checks, Network Access Analyzer scopes, and Network Manager Route Analyzer for transit gateway paths. Covers Traffic Mirroring and its key limit: it is not supported on Nitro v5 or v6 instances (for example M8g, M9g, C8i), so current-generation sources need host packet capture, GWLB-based inspection or extended flow-log fields instead. Hybrid paths are in troubleshooting-hybrid-and-private-connectivity, logging design in network-logging-monitoring-and-audit, and CloudWatch network monitoring in cloud/aws/observability. Ends with an exam-shortcuts box linking reference/aws-networking-cheatsheet.

articles.title: Network cost on AWS: data transfer, NAT processing, cross-AZ traffic, endpoints, public IPv4 and how to reduce them
articles.scope: Models the main network cost drivers: internet egress, inter-Region and inter-AZ transfer, NAT gateway processing, Transit Gateway data processing (and Flexible Cost Allocation), interface endpoint hours, and public IPv4 charges. Shows ways to cut them: gateway endpoints, CloudFront, AZ affinity, Direct Connect, and the CloudFront and Direct Connect flat-rate plans. Links to cloud/aws/cost for billing tooling.

articles.title: Automating AWS networks: IaC patterns in CloudFormation, CDK and Terraform, parameterized addressing, event-driven network automation and drift
articles.scope: Builds a multi-account network with CloudFormation, CDK (C# and Python) and Terraform, and shows the problems hardcoding causes (CIDRs, AZ names, account IDs). Replaces literals with IPAM allocations, managed prefix lists, SSM parameters and AZ IDs. Adds event-driven automation with EventBridge and Lambda (for example, auto-attaching new VPCs to a transit gateway or updating prefix lists from published IP ranges), CLI and SDK scripting, and drift detection. StackSets and Guard depth link to cloud/aws/iac-devops, and neutral IaC concepts to devops/iac.

articles.title: Overlapping IP address space on AWS: private NAT gateway vs PrivateLink vs VPC Lattice vs Transit Gateway 1:1 NAT vs non-routable secondary CIDRs vs re-IP
articles.scope: A decision guide for networks that overlap after acquisitions, partner integrations or careless planning. Compares re-addressing, PrivateLink or Lattice service-level connectivity, private NAT gateways with routable and non-routable secondary CIDRs, transit gateway 1:1 NAT (22 Oct 2026) and appliance-based NAT, on scale, direction of initiation, DNS impact, cost and operability. Includes reference diagrams and IPAM-based prevention. Maps to Azure Virtual WAN NAT rules and VPN Gateway NAT (partial).

articles.title: Network logging, monitoring and audit: flow-log fields, ELB, CloudFront, WAF, Resolver and Network Firewall logs, delivery options, and multi-account network audits
articles.scope: Defines logging and monitoring requirements and a traffic baseline. Covers VPC and transit gateway flow-log base vs extended fields, ELB access and connection logs, CloudFront standard logging v2 and real-time logs, WAF logs, VPC Resolver query logs and Network Firewall alert and flow logs, and how each is delivered (S3, CloudWatch Logs, Firehose). Correlates them with Athena and CloudWatch Logs Insights. Audits multi-account network posture with Firewall Manager, Config rules, Network Access Analyzer and Trusted Advisor. CloudWatch network monitoring features link to cloud/aws/observability. Maps to Azure VNet flow logs, Traffic Analytics and diagnostic settings (close).

articles.title: Troubleshooting hybrid and private connectivity: VPN tunnel, IKE and BGP states, Direct Connect VIF and BGP down, asymmetric routing, route priority, Resolver endpoint and PrivateLink DNS failures
articles.scope: A runbook for failures that cross the VPC edge: VPN tunnel status and IKE phase 1 and 2 mismatches, dead peer detection, BGP session down or routes not received, Direct Connect physical and VIF states, BGP route limits, asymmetric routing and route priority surprises between Direct Connect, VPN and static routes, MTU mismatches over tunnels, and Resolver endpoint, forwarding-rule and PrivateLink private DNS failures. Uses CloudWatch tunnel and VIF metrics, VPN logs, Route Analyzer and Reachability Analyzer. Maps to Azure VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute diagnostics (close).

articles.title: Troubleshooting CloudFront caching: cache keys and cache policies, TTL precedence, invalidation vs versioned names, cache-hit ratio, origin errors and logs
articles.scope: Diagnoses low hit ratios and stale or wrong content: cache-key design with cache and origin request policies, TTL precedence with Cache-Control and Expires, invalidation vs versioned object names (as an Angular build does), Origin Shield, origin 4xx and 5xx responses, timeouts and error caching, and custom error pages. Uses the CacheHitRate and error-rate metrics, standard logging v2 and real-time logs. Maps to Azure Front Door caching rules and purge (close).

articles.title: AWS global infrastructure: Regions, AZs and AZ IDs, partitions, edge locations, Local Zones, Wavelength Zones and Outposts
articles.scope: Explains Regions (and opt-in Regions), AZs and why AZ names differ from AZ IDs between accounts, and the partitions (commercial, GovCloud, China and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud, documented at docs.aws.eu) and how they affect ARNs, endpoints and identity. Covers AWS Global View (renamed from EC2 Global View, 30 Jun 2026), edge locations and Regional edge caches, and compares Local Zones, Dedicated Local Zones, Wavelength Zones and Outposts racks and servers, with selection criteria for latency, residency and DR. Links cloud/foundations for the neutral Region and zone concepts. Maps to Azure regions, availability zones, Extended Zones and Azure Local.

articles.title: Amazon EC2 fundamentals: instances, lifecycle, user data, ENIs, status checks and recovery
articles.scope: Covers launching from an AMI with a launch template, key pairs, user data and cloud-init or EC2Launch, and the instance lifecycle (stop, hibernate, terminate, termination protection). Explains ENIs and Elastic IPs, system, instance and attached-EBS status checks, simplified automatic recovery, and hibernation as a cost lever for non-production instances (with Instance Scheduler on AWS). Includes C# and Python SDK launch samples plus Bicep-vs-CloudFormation-vs-Terraform equivalents.

articles.title: EC2 instance types and sizing: families, the naming convention, Graviton vs Intel vs AMD, burstable credits and rightsizing
articles.scope: Decodes instance names (family, generation, processor, attributes, size), the general-purpose, compute-, memory-, storage-optimized, accelerated and HPC families, Graviton4 and Graviton5 (M9g/M9gd, C9g/C9gd, R9g/R9gd on Nitro v6, 2026), the Nitro version per family, flex instances, and burstable CPU credits with unlimited mode. Covers rightsizing with Compute Optimizer and CloudWatch metrics, and maps families to Azure VM series.

articles.title: EC2 purchasing options: On-Demand vs Savings Plans vs Reserved Instances vs Spot vs Dedicated, Capacity Reservations and Capacity Blocks
articles.scope: Compares commitment, discount, flexibility and capacity assurance from the EC2 point of view; the commitment portfolio and discount order live in cloud/aws/cost. Covers Compute vs EC2 Instance Savings Plans, Standard vs Convertible and regional vs zonal RIs, Spot (interruption notice, rebalance recommendations, allocation strategies), Dedicated Hosts vs Dedicated Instances for licensing, and ODCRs including future-dated and interruptible (21 Nov 2025). States the Capacity Blocks for ML rules: 1-14 days or multiples of 7 days up to 182 days, start up to 8 weeks ahead, no cancellation, no placement groups, up to 64 instances per block and 256 across blocks, sharing within an organization (Feb 2026). Adds EC2 Capacity Manager (Oct 2025) for multi-account capacity visibility, and RI and Savings Plans sharing. Maps to Azure reservations, savings plan for compute and Spot VMs.

articles.title: AMIs and image governance: EBS-backed vs instance-store-backed, sharing, encryption, Allowed AMIs, watermarks and EC2 Image Builder
articles.scope: Builds a golden-image pipeline with EC2 Image Builder. Covers AMI copy and encryption across Regions and accounts, sharing and block public access for AMIs, deprecation, ancestry and usage reports, and enforcing Allowed AMIs (including 2026 watermarks) through declarative policies and Config. Maps to Azure Compute Gallery and VM Image Builder.

articles.title: Block storage for EC2: EBS volume types, snapshots, encryption and performance vs instance store
articles.scope: Compares gp3 (up to 64 TiB, 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MiB/s since 26 Sep 2025), gp2, io2 Block Express, io1, st1 and sc1 with ephemeral NVMe instance store. Covers EBS-optimized throughput, Elastic Volumes (since 15 Jan 2026 a new modification can start as soon as the previous one completes, up to four times in 24 hours), Multi-Attach, encryption by default, and instant point-in-time volume copy (14 Oct 2025). Covers snapshots: incremental, time-based snapshot and AMI copies, Fast Snapshot Restore vs Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization (May 2025), archive, snapshot lock (WORM), Recycle Bin for snapshots, AMIs and EBS volumes (20 Nov 2025), and DLM vs AWS Backup (backup-plan depth in cloud/aws/storage-data). Ends with diagnosing performance from CloudWatch metrics. Maps to Azure Managed Disks and temporary disks.

articles.title: The Nitro System, enhanced networking and placement groups: performance and isolation under the hood
articles.scope: Explains Nitro cards, the Nitro hypervisor, the Nitro security chip and the Nitro versions (v2 to v6) with what each changes: Nitro v5 and v6 drop Traffic Mirroring support, and Nitro v6 cuts the default established TCP idle timeout to 350 s and offers up to 400 Gbps per network card. Covers Nitro Enclaves, NitroTPM, AMD SEV-SNP and bare metal. Covers ENA, ENA Express (including cross-AZ), EFA and per-instance bandwidth limits, and the cluster, partition, spread and precision-time placement strategies with their limits. Maps to Azure Boost, Accelerated Networking, confidential VMs and proximity placement groups.

articles.title: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling: launch templates, scaling policies, warm pools, lifecycle hooks, instance refresh and mixed instances
articles.scope: Covers Auto Scaling groups across AZs, launch templates vs the deprecated launch configurations, and target tracking, step, simple, scheduled and predictive scaling. Explains health checks and grace periods, default instance warmup, termination policies, warm pools, lifecycle hooks, instance refresh, mixed instances with attribute-based selection, Spot capacity rebalancing, and ELB integration with zonal shift. Maps to VM Scale Sets. Contrasts with Application Auto Scaling, scaling plans and EC2 Fleet in aws-scaling-services-compared.

articles.title: Secure EC2 access: IMDSv2 enforcement, instance profiles, EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint, Session Manager and the serial console
articles.scope: Hardens instance access: requiring IMDSv2 and hop limits (account-level enforcement since February 2026), the ImdsV1Enabled metric, instance profiles instead of keys, EC2 Instance Connect and Instance Connect Endpoint vs Systems Manager Session Manager vs bastions, and the serial console. Maps to Azure Bastion, JIT VM access and Azure IMDS.

articles.title: Choosing AWS compute: EC2 vs Lambda vs Fargate/ECS (including ECS Express Mode) vs EKS vs Elastic Beanstalk vs Lightsail vs Batch vs VMware
articles.scope: A decision guide covering control, operational burden, scaling granularity, cold start, cost model, statefulness and licensing for each platform. Marks AWS App Runner as legacy (closed to new customers on 2026-04-30; existing customers only) and presents Amazon ECS Express Mode as AWS's recommended replacement, linked to cloud/aws/containers. Adds a VMware option (VMware Cloud on AWS, on the SAA-C03 in-scope list, and Amazon Elastic VMware Service) with a link to architecture/migration. Points to the containers and serverless sections for depth, and pairs each option with its nearest Azure counterpart (VMs, Functions, Container Apps, AKS, App Service, Batch, Azure VMware Solution) and a fidelity rating.

articles.title: Licensing on AWS: license-included vs BYOL, Dedicated Hosts and host resource groups, AWS License Manager and Optimize CPUs for Windows Server and SQL Server
articles.scope: Explains license-included vs bring-your-own-license economics (the CLF-C02 1.4.5 skill), which Microsoft licenses need Dedicated Hosts, and how host resource groups and AWS License Manager rules track and enforce usage. Covers Optimize CPUs to cut per-core licensing, Windows Server and SQL Server on EC2 options, and License Manager reporting across an organization. Links architecture/cost and cloud/aws/cost. Maps to Azure Hybrid Benefit and Azure Dedicated Host (partial).

articles.title: Scaling services compared: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling vs Application Auto Scaling vs AWS Auto Scaling scaling plans vs EC2 Fleet and Spot Fleet
articles.scope: Sets out which engine scales what: EC2 Auto Scaling for instance groups, Application Auto Scaling for ECS, DynamoDB, Aurora replicas, Spot Fleet and more, AWS Auto Scaling scaling plans across resources, and EC2 Fleet and Spot Fleet as fleet APIs with allocation strategies, attribute-based instance type selection and Capacity Reservation targeting. Explains AWS's guidance to prefer predictive scaling policies set directly on Auto Scaling groups over scaling plans (with its migration guide) and to prefer Auto Scaling groups or EC2 Fleet over the legacy Spot Fleet API. Maps to VM Scale Sets and Azure Monitor autoscale (partial).

articles.title: AWS Batch, ParallelCluster, Parallel Computing Service and EMR: Batch, HPC and Big-Data Compute
articles.scope: Wave 2. Compares the AWS options for non-interactive compute. AWS Batch runs compute environments on EC2, Spot, Fargate or EKS, with job queues, fair-share scheduling, array jobs and multi-node parallel jobs. For Slurm-based HPC it compares open-source AWS ParallelCluster (cluster config YAML, EFA, FSx for Lustre) with the managed AWS Parallel Computing Service. For Spark and Hadoop it compares EMR on EC2, EMR on EKS and EMR Serverless, with Glue as the serverless ETL alternative. Spot for batch covers capacity-optimized allocation, interruption notices and checkpointing. Decision rules are given for SAA-C03 3.2.1 and 3.5.12. It mirrors azure-batch-and-hpc-options (Azure Batch, CycleCloud) and carries a difference row: Azure Batch vs AWS Batch (close), CycleCloud vs ParallelCluster (close).

articles.title: Systems Manager hybrid nodes: managing on-premises and multicloud servers from AWS
articles.scope: Counterpart of azure-arc-and-hybrid-servers. Hybrid activations and the SSM Agent, the unified Systems Manager console, Patch Manager, State Manager, Run Command, Session Manager and Inventory on non-EC2 machines; EKS Hybrid Nodes and ECS Anywhere for containers; what Arc does that AWS has no equivalent for, namely projecting resources into the control plane for Policy and RBAC.

terms.definition: A transit gateway VPN option that enters the AWS network at the nearest edge location through Global Accelerator, reducing internet path variability.

Control Tower's account-vending capability, built on Service Catalog, that creates and enrolls accounts with a standard baseline; Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) offers the same through a GitOps Terraform pipeline.
An Organizations declarative policy that controls, across accounts, whether AWS AI services may store and use customer content to improve those services.
An account-level EC2 setting, enforceable by declarative policy, that limits which AMIs can be discovered and launched by provider, name, age, Marketplace code or (since 2026) provenance watermark.
An AWS service for application recovery that provides zonal shift and zonal autoshift away from an impaired AZ, routing controls with readiness checks, and orchestrated Region switch plans.
aliases: formerly: Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller

terms.definition: AWS's content delivery network that caches and accelerates HTTP(S), WebSocket and gRPC traffic at edge locations, with cache and origin policies, edge functions, signed URLs and AWS WAF integration.
Network-attached, AZ-scoped persistent block volumes for EC2 in SSD types (gp3, gp2, io2 Block Express, io1) and HDD types (st1, sc1); gp3 scales to 64 TiB, 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MiB/s.
AWS's virtual server service that provides resizable instances of many types, launched from AMIs into VPC subnets and billed per second or hour depending on OS.
A Regional template of root volume snapshots, block device mappings and launch permissions used to launch instances; it can be copied, encrypted, shared and deprecated.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Compute Gallery image version (close)

terms.definition: The globally unique identifier format for AWS resources (arn:partition:service:region:account-id:resource) used in policies, APIs and IaC.
AWS's highly available DNS service, combining authoritative public and private hosted zones, domain registration, health checks and traffic routing policies.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure DNS plus Traffic Manager (partial)

terms.definition: A managed fine-grained authorization service that evaluates application permissions written in the open-source Cedar policy language, separating authorization logic from application code.
A logically isolated, Region-scoped virtual network in an AWS account, defined by IPv4 and optional IPv6 CIDR blocks, in which AZ-scoped subnets, route tables and gateways are created.

A managed application-networking service that connects, secures (with IAM auth policies) and monitors services and TCP resources across VPCs and accounts through service networks, independent of IP routing.

The scaling engine for resources other than EC2 instance groups, such as ECS services, DynamoDB tables, Aurora replicas, Spot Fleet, Lambda provisioned concurrency and SageMaker endpoints, with target tracking, step and scheduled policies.
A layer 7 load balancer for HTTP, HTTPS and gRPC with content-based listener rules, TLS termination, mTLS, OIDC user authentication, JWT access-token validation, and instance, IP or Lambda targets.

Describing required vCPU, memory and other attributes instead of listing instance types, so Auto Scaling groups and EC2 Fleet pick from every matching type, including new ones, which diversifies Spot capacity.

An Auto Scaling hook that pauses an instance in a Pending:Wait or Terminating:Wait state, so custom actions such as configuration, log drain or deregistration can run before it enters or leaves service.
A pool of pre-initialized stopped, hibernated or running instances kept beside an Auto Scaling group, so scale-out skips long boot and bootstrap times.

Writing IAM policies that grant access when principal tags match resource or request tags (aws:PrincipalTag, aws:ResourceTag, aws:RequestTag), so permissions scale without a new policy for every team or resource.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure ABAC role assignment conditions (partial)

terms.definition: The identity created with an AWS account and signed in with the account email address; it has full access in its account unless SCPs or RCPs limit it (member accounts), and it is the only identity that can perform a small set of tasks such as closing the account or changing the support plan. With centralized root access a member account may have no root credentials at all, and root tasks run through sts:AssumeRoot.

AWS's Envoy-based managed service mesh for ECS, EKS and EC2, still on the ANS-C01 in-scope list but discontinued on 30 Sep 2026, when its console and resources stopped being accessible; ECS workloads migrate to ECS Service Connect.
terms.equivalent: azure: Istio-based service mesh add-on for AKS (partial)

terms.definition: A plan in the AWS Auto Scaling console that discovers scalable resources of an application and applies target tracking and predictive scaling across them; AWS now recommends predictive scaling policies set directly on Auto Scaling groups and publishes a migration guide.
A managed OpenVPN-based remote-access service that authenticates users with certificates, Active Directory or SAML and places them on VPC networks; native transit gateway attachment arrived in 2026.
A service-discovery registry where applications register service instances with attributes and health and look them up by API or DNS; it underpins ECS Service Connect.
terms.equivalent: azure: none native (partial: Azure Container Apps and AKS built-in discovery)

terms.definition: A managed global WAN service in which a JSON core network policy defines segments, core network edges per Region, attachment rules and service insertion, replacing hand-built transit gateway peering meshes.
The AWS service that records API activity and account actions as events, giving an audit history of who did what, from where and when.
An AWS service that analyzes utilization metrics to recommend rightsizing for EC2 instances, Auto Scaling groups, EBS volumes, Lambda functions and other resources.
The AWS service that records resource configurations and their changes over time and evaluates them continuously against rules and conformance packs, with optional automatic remediation.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy compliance plus Resource Graph change analysis (partial)

terms.definition: An AWS Config resource that collects configuration and compliance data from multiple accounts and Regions, or a whole organization, into one account for central queries.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Resource Graph cross-subscription queries (close)

terms.definition: A point-in-time record that AWS Config creates of a resource's attributes, relationships and metadata whenever the configuration recorder detects a change.
terms.equivalent: azure: Resource Graph resource change record (close)

terms.definition: A deployable collection of Config rules and remediation actions, such as an operational best practices pack for a framework, applied to an account or across an organization.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy initiative / regulatory compliance (close)

terms.definition: A desired-state check, either AWS managed or custom (Lambda or Guard), evaluated when configurations change, periodically, or proactively before provisioning, which marks resources compliant or non-compliant.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy definition with audit effect (close)

terms.definition: Global condition keys that tie an AWS service principal's request to the resource, account, organization or OU it acts for, and flag requests made by service principals, so resource policies, trust policies and RCPs can stop one service from being used against another customer's resources.
The AWS catalog (renamed in June 2025) of managed controls with their objectives, domains, behaviors and framework mappings, which Control Tower and other services use to find and enable controls.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy built-in definitions and regulatory compliance initiatives (partial)

terms.definition: The AWS service that sets up and governs a multi-account landing zone by orchestrating Organizations, IAM Identity Center, Config and CloudTrail, with managed controls, drift detection and Account Factory.
A set of preventive guardrails, built with SCPs, RCPs, resource-based and VPC endpoint policies, that allows only trusted identities to access trusted resources from expected networks.
terms.equivalent: azure: Private Link plus network security perimeter plus tenant restrictions (partial)

terms.definition: A dedicated or partner-hosted private network connection from on-premises to an AWS Direct Connect location that gives consistent bandwidth and latency; it is not encrypted by default, and MACsec or IPsec is added on top.

The AWS family of directory options: AWS Managed Microsoft AD (a real, AWS-managed AD forest that supports trusts), AD Connector (a proxy to on-premises AD), and Simple AD (a Samba-based, AD-compatible directory).
An AWS point of presence outside the Regions that serves CloudFront, Route 53, Global Accelerator and Shield, backed by larger Regional edge caches for CloudFront.
An organization-wide policy service that centrally deploys and audits AWS WAF, Shield Advanced, security group, Network Firewall, DNS Firewall and third-party firewall policies across accounts.

A network-layer service that gives two static anycast IPv4 addresses (or four, dual-stack) entering the AWS backbone at the nearest edge and routing TCP/UDP to healthy Regional endpoints, without caching; since CloudFront also offers Anycast static IPs, static IPs alone no longer decide between the two.

AWS-designed Arm64 processors that power the g-suffixed instance families; Graviton5 families M9g/M9gd, C9g/C9gd and R9g/R9gd (2026) run on Nitro v6, while Graviton4 families such as M8g run on Nitro v5, and Graviton usually gives better price-performance than x86 for Linux workloads.

The AWS view of service events and account-specific events (scheduled changes, retirements, issues affecting your resources), also available through the AWS Health API and EventBridge, with an organizational view that aggregates events across accounts.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Service Health and Resource Health (close)

terms.definition: The AWS workforce identity service that connects an identity source, gives single sign-on to AWS accounts and applications, and grants account access through permission sets assigned to users and groups.
terms.equivalent: azure: Microsoft Entra ID SSO plus Azure RBAC assignments (partial)

terms.definition: A managed private Layer 3 connection with MACsec-encrypted physical links between AWS and other cloud providers, billed hourly by capacity; when checked, the product page showed Microsoft Azure in preview and OCI planned, and Google Cloud general availability could not be confirmed from a primary source.
terms.equivalent: azure: none native; closest is ExpressRoute through colocation or cloud-exchange partners (partial)

terms.definition: A pre-configured, governed multi-account AWS environment with baseline identity, logging, security and network accounts and guardrails, usually built with Control Tower or Landing Zone Accelerator.

An AWS service that tracks software licenses through license configurations and rules (cores, sockets, instances), enforces limits at launch, manages host resource groups for Dedicated Hosts, and reports usage across an organization.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Hybrid Benefit tracking in Cost Management (partial)

terms.definition: An extension of a Region placed in a metropolitan area that runs a subset of services, such as EC2, EBS and ELB, for single-digit-millisecond latency or local data residency; Dedicated Local Zones are built for a single customer.
A standalone identity-based policy that AWS creates and updates, such as ReadOnlyAccess, which customers can attach but not edit.

The maximum packet sizes on AWS paths: 9001 bytes inside a VPC and over intra-Region peering, 8500 through NAT gateways, transit gateways and Direct Connect transit VIFs, 1500 to the internet and less over VPN tunnels; mismatches cause hangs on large packets.
terms.equivalent: azure: VNet MTU 1500 by default, configurable up to 4000 (partial)

terms.definition: A managed, stateful network firewall and IPS for VPC traffic, with stateless and Suricata-compatible stateful rule engines, domain filtering, TLS inspection and managed threat rules, deployed via endpoints or transit gateway attachments.
The AWS service, with its own user guide since 2021, that gives a global view of transit gateways, Cloud WAN, on-premises sites and links, with topology, events, metrics and Route Analyzer.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Virtual Network Manager and Network Watcher topology (partial)

terms.definition: Isolated compute environments carved from an EC2 instance's CPU and memory, with no persistent storage, interactive access or external networking, and cryptographic attestation integrated with KMS for processing highly sensitive data.

AWS's virtualization platform of dedicated Nitro cards for networking, storage and management, the Nitro security chip and a lightweight Nitro hypervisor, which isolates customer workloads and allows no operator access to them; Nitro versions v2 to v6 differ in network features (v5 and v6 drop Traffic Mirroring support).

The AWS service that groups accounts into a hierarchy under one management account, providing consolidated billing, organization policies, trusted access and delegated administration for integrated services.
terms.equivalent: azure: tenant root plus management group hierarchy (close)

terms.definition: AWS-owned and AWS-managed racks or servers installed on customer premises that extend a Region's AZ, running EC2, EBS, ECS, EKS, RDS and S3 on Outposts with the same APIs, connected through a service link.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Local (formerly Azure Stack HCI) (partial)

terms.definition: A separate group of Regions with its own identities, endpoints and ARN prefix: the commercial partition, AWS GovCloud (US), the China Regions and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud; credentials and many features do not cross partitions.

A global condition key holding the AWS Organizations ID of the calling principal's account, used in resource-based policies to allow access to the whole organization without listing account IDs; the separate key aws:PrincipalOrgPaths matches the principal's OU path.

The AWS technology for exposing a service (behind an NLB or GWLB) or resource privately to consumer VPCs through interface or resource endpoints, with one-way connectivity and no need for non-overlapping CIDRs.
A separate geographic area containing multiple isolated Availability Zones, which most AWS services are scoped to; newer Regions must be opted in before use.

The AWS service that shares supported resources, such as subnets, transit gateways, Resolver rules, prefix lists and capacity reservations, with other accounts, OUs or the whole organization without copying them.
terms.equivalent: azure: cross-subscription RBAC plus Azure Lighthouse (partial)

terms.term: AWS Resource Groups and Tag Editor
terms.definition: Tools to group resources by tag or CloudFormation stack and to find and bulk-edit tags across Regions; AWS Resource Explorer adds cross-Region and cross-account resource search.
terms.equivalent: azure: resource groups plus Azure Resource Graph search (partial)

terms.definition: A case-sensitive key-value label attached to an AWS resource, used for organization, automation, cost allocation and tag-based access control.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure resource tag (close; AWS tag keys and values are case-sensitive while Azure tag names are not, and Azure can inherit tags by policy)

terms.definition: An AWS service that lets administrators publish approved CloudFormation- or Terraform-based products with constraints, so users can self-provision compliant resources and accounts.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure managed applications service catalog / template specs (partial)

terms.definition: The hostname an SDK or CLI calls for a service: regional (service.region.amazonaws.com), global for a few services such as IAM, FIPS-validated variants and dual-stack (IPv6) variants; feature availability can differ, as with STS GetWebIdentityToken, which the global STS endpoint does not serve.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Resource Manager and service endpoints per cloud (partial)

terms.definition: A paid subscription adding enhanced DDoS detection and mitigation for protected resources, Shield Response Team access, health-based detection and cost protection; from 26 Mar 2026 the AWS WAF Anti-DDoS managed rule group is the default HTTP-flood protection and supersedes Shield Advanced Layer 7 Auto Mitigation, which existing customers may keep and new customers can get only through AWS Support.
Automatic, no-cost protection for all AWS customers against common layer 3 and 4 DDoS attacks on AWS edge and Regional services.
A managed IPsec VPN service in which each connection provides two tunnels between a customer gateway and a virtual private gateway, transit gateway or Cloud WAN, using static or BGP routing.

A global condition key containing the ID of the VPC endpoint a request arrived through; related but separate keys are aws:SourceVpc (the VPC) and, since 2025, aws:VpceAccount, aws:VpceOrgID and aws:VpceOrgPaths, which match the endpoint owner's account, organization or OU.
terms.equivalent: azure: storage firewall rules for private endpoints and VNets (partial)

terms.definition: The AWS service that issues temporary, limited-lifetime credentials through APIs such as AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithSAML, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity and GetSessionToken.
terms.equivalent: azure: Microsoft Entra ID token endpoint (partial)

terms.definition: AWS's support tiers: free Basic plus the paid Business Support+, Enterprise and Unified Operations plans, which add faster response times, full Trusted Advisor checks and named technical contacts; legacy Developer and Business plans closed to new subscriptions on 2 Dec 2025 and run until 1 Jan 2027.

A regional, managed hub router that connects VPCs, VPNs, Direct Connect gateways, SD-WAN (Connect) and peered transit gateways through attachments and multiple route tables, enabling transitive routing at scale.

An AWS service that inspects accounts and recommends improvements in cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits and operational excellence; full checks require a Business-tier or higher plan (Business Support+, Enterprise or Unified Operations, or legacy Business and Enterprise On-Ramp until they retire).

A zero-trust access service that evaluates each connection against identity and device-posture policies before granting access to applications, including non-HTTP resources such as SSH, RDP and databases, without a VPN.

A layer 7 web application firewall whose web ACLs (shown as protection packs in the new console) apply managed and custom rules, rate limits, Bot Control and fraud-control rules to CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito and other resources.
AWS compute and storage embedded in telecommunications providers' 5G networks, reached through a carrier gateway for ultra-low-latency mobile edge applications.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Operator Nexus / private MEC (partial)

terms.definition: An EC2 T-family instance that earns CPU credits below a baseline and spends them to burst; in unlimited mode it can exceed its credits for an extra charge.
terms.equivalent: azure: B-series VMs (close; B-series bank credits too, but T-instance unlimited mode has no B-series twin)

terms.definition: Bringing a publicly routable IPv4 or IPv6 range you own to AWS through IPAM, to advertise for EC2 Elastic IPs, Global Accelerator and, since November 2025, CloudFront, keeping allow-listed addresses during migration.
The VPC gateway for Wavelength Zone subnets that allows inbound traffic from the telecom carrier network and translates outbound traffic to carrier IP addresses.

An IAM and Organizations capability (November 2024) for removing member accounts' root credentials and performing scoped privileged root tasks from the management or delegated account, without root passwords.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra PIM for Global Administrator (partial)

terms.definition: A dedicated set of static anycast IP addresses for a CloudFront distribution (November 2024; dual-stack and BYOIP through IPAM, November 2025) for clients and firewalls that must allow-list IPs, which removes a classic reason to choose Global Accelerator.

The values CloudFront uses to identify a cached object (domain, path and whichever query strings, headers and cookies the cache policy includes); an origin request policy forwards extra values to the origin without adding them to the cache key.
terms.equivalent: azure: Front Door caching rules and query string behavior (close)

terms.definition: A third CloudFront function type (November 2025) that runs during the TLS handshake of viewer mTLS connections to inspect client certificates and allow or deny the connection.

CloudFront's two request/response edge-compute options: CloudFront Functions are sub-millisecond JavaScript for viewer request/response manipulation at every edge location, and Lambda@Edge runs Node.js or Python at Regional edge caches with network access, longer runtimes and origin events; Connection Functions, a separate third type, run during viewer mTLS.

A no-overage monthly plan (November 2025) that bundles CloudFront delivery with AWS WAF, DDoS protection, Route 53 DNS, CloudWatch Logs ingestion, edge compute and S3 credits; blocked attack traffic does not count against usage.

terms.term: CloudFront standard logging v2 and real-time logs
terms.definition: CloudFront's request logs: standard logging v2 (November 2024) delivers access logs to CloudWatch Logs, Firehose or S3, while real-time logs stream sampled fields to Kinesis Data Streams within seconds.
terms.equivalent: azure: Front Door access logs via diagnostic settings (close)

terms.definition: The CloudFront mechanism that SigV4-signs origin requests so that S3 buckets (including SSE-KMS buckets), Lambda function URLs and MediaPackage origins accept only requests from specific distributions.
terms.equivalent: azure: Front Door Private Link origins / managed identity to storage (partial)

terms.definition: An optional extra caching layer in one chosen Regional edge cache that collapses requests from all edge locations, raising hit ratio and cutting origin load and cost.
terms.equivalent: azure: Front Door origin shielding via caching tiers (partial)

terms.term: CloudFront signed URLs and signed cookies
terms.definition: Ways to restrict private content: a signed URL grants access to one object, while signed cookies grant access to many objects without changing URLs; both are signed with keys in a trusted key group.
terms.equivalent: azure: Front Door token authentication with rules or SAS on origin (partial)

terms.definition: A CloudFront origin type (November 2024) that reaches ALBs, NLBs or EC2 instances in private subnets directly, so the origin needs no public exposure; it can be shared across accounts via RAM.
terms.equivalent: azure: Front Door Premium Private Link origin (close)

terms.definition: CloudTrail's event categories: management events (control-plane), data events (resource data-plane operations such as S3 object access), network activity events (API calls through VPC endpoints) and Insights events (anomalous API rates or errors).
terms.equivalent: azure: Activity Log vs resource logs (partial)

terms.definition: A managed store and SQL query engine for CloudTrail and other activity events, closed to new customers from 2026-05-31 while existing customers continue to use it; new estates use an organization trail to S3 with Athena, CloudWatch Logs Insights or Security Lake instead.
terms.equivalent: azure: Log Analytics workspace with Activity Log (partial)

terms.definition: A CloudTrail feature that writes signed SHA-256 digest files, so you can prove that delivered log files were not modified or deleted after delivery.

A CloudTrail trail created in the management or delegated administrator account that logs events for every account in the organization, typically to a central Log Archive bucket that member accounts cannot modify.
terms.equivalent: azure: management-group diagnostic settings via Azure Policy (partial)

terms.definition: A Cognito component that exchanges tokens from user pools, social IdPs or SAML providers (or guest access) for temporary AWS credentials mapped to IAM roles.
A managed user directory and OIDC/OAuth 2.0 authorization server for application end users, with sign-up, sign-in, MFA, social and enterprise federation, and JWT issuance.
The Organizations feature that combines all member accounts' charges into one bill, aggregating usage for volume pricing tiers and sharing Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts.
terms.equivalent: azure: billing account with billing profiles (partial)

terms.definition: A Control Tower governance rule that is preventive (SCP, RCP or declarative policy), detective (Config rule) or proactive (CloudFormation hook), with mandatory, strongly recommended or elective guidance.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy assignments in a landing zone (close)

terms.definition: A divergence between a Control Tower landing zone's expected configuration and its actual state, such as an account moved between OUs or a modified managed SCP; Control Tower finds it with daily scans of managed SCPs, RCPs and declarative policies and reports it in the console and through SNS notifications aggregated in the audit account, and drift status is also returned programmatically for enabled baselines.
A resource tag that is activated in the Billing console so that it appears as a dimension in Cost Explorer and cost and usage reports; it can be user-defined or AWS-generated.

A load balancer setting that spreads traffic evenly across all registered targets in every enabled AZ rather than per-AZ; it is on by default for ALB, off by default for NLB and GWLB, and inter-AZ charges can apply.
The AWS resource that represents the customer's on-premises VPN device: its public IP (or certificate) and BGP ASN.
terms.equivalent: azure: local network gateway (close; the Azure object also holds the on-premises address prefixes, while AWS keeps routes in the VPN connection)

terms.definition: A standalone, versioned identity-based policy that a customer authors in its own account and can attach to many identities.

An AWS solution that applies CloudFormation templates and SCPs from a pipeline to Control Tower accounts on lifecycle events such as account creation, used where Account Factory baselines are not enough.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Landing Zones subscription vending customizations (partial)

terms.definition: The Organizations policy category enforced in a service's control plane rather than at API authorization, maintaining a baseline configuration even as new APIs appear; unlike SCPs and RCPs it affects the management account, governs service-linked roles, shows an effective policy per account and rolls back on detach. Types include Amazon EC2, Backup, Tag, Chat applications, AI services opt-out, Security Hub, Inspector, Bedrock, Upgrade rollout, S3, Shield network security director and GuardDuty.

A physical EC2 server fully dedicated to one account, with visibility into sockets and cores and control over instance placement, supporting bring-your-own-license for per-socket or per-core software.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Dedicated Host (close; AWS adds host resource groups and License Manager integration, Azure uses host groups with fault domains)

terms.definition: An EC2 instance that runs on hardware dedicated to one account but without host-level visibility or placement control, used for tenancy compliance rather than licensing.

The VPC AWS pre-creates in each Region of a new account (172.31.0.0/16 with a public subnet per AZ, an internet gateway and default security group and NACL), convenient for tests but usually deleted or replaced in governed accounts; it can be recreated with CreateDefaultVpc.

A member account registered to administer an integrated service (for example GuardDuty, Config or IAM Identity Center) for the whole organization, keeping day-to-day operations out of the management account.
The time a load balancer keeps sending in-flight requests to a target being deregistered before closing it (300 s by default), so scale-in and deployments do not cut active connections.
terms.equivalent: azure: Application Gateway connection draining (close; Azure applies one drain timeout per backend setting, ELB per target group)

terms.definition: A VPC configuration of the domain name, DNS servers, NTP servers and NetBIOS settings handed to instances by DHCP; replacing AmazonProvidedDNS with custom servers changes hybrid DNS behavior.

BGP community tags for steering Direct Connect traffic: 7224:7100, 7224:7200 and 7224:7300 set low, medium and high local preference for return paths, 7224:9100, 9200 and 9300 limit public VIF prefix scope to the local Region, continent or globe, and NO_EXPORT is honored.
terms.equivalent: azure: ExpressRoute route filters and BGP communities (partial)

terms.definition: A globally available construct that links private or transit VIFs to virtual private gateways or transit gateways in any commercial Region; it does not route traffic between the VPCs attached to it.
terms.equivalent: azure: ExpressRoute circuit with Premium / Global Reach (partial)

terms.definition: A Direct Connect connection provisioned by a partner on its own port at a chosen speed, which supports one VIF; a dedicated connection is a physical port of your own that supports many VIFs, LAGs and MACsec.
terms.equivalent: azure: ExpressRoute provider circuit vs ExpressRoute Direct (close)

terms.definition: A bundle of same-speed dedicated connections at one Direct Connect location, managed with LACP as a single logical connection, with a minimum-links setting.

The colocation facility where AWS Direct Connect routers live, and the Letter of Authorization and Connecting Facility Assignment that AWS issues so you or a partner can order the cross-connect to the assigned port.
terms.equivalent: azure: ExpressRoute peering location and LOA (close)

terms.definition: The limits and filters on routes over Direct Connect: 100 routes per BGP session on private and transit VIFs by default (up to 1,000 with prefix controls), 1,000 on public VIFs, and the allowed-prefixes list on a Direct Connect gateway association that controls what AWS advertises.
terms.equivalent: azure: ExpressRoute route limits and route filters (partial)

terms.definition: A per-VIF bandwidth cap (2026), with up to 10 rate limiters per dedicated connection, that stops one VIF from starving others on a shared port.

The Resiliency Toolkit's patterns: maximum (separate connections on separate devices at two or more locations), high (one connection at each of two locations) and development and test (two connections at one location).
A Direct Connect feature that sends traffic between your sites over the AWS backbone through Direct Connect locations, without passing through a Region.
