A VLAN with a BGP session on a Direct Connect connection: a private VIF reaches VPCs, a public VIF reaches AWS public endpoints, and a transit VIF reaches transit gateways through a Direct Connect gateway.

Changing an EBS volume's size, type, IOPS or throughput while it stays attached; since 15 Jan 2026 a new modification can start as soon as the previous one completes, up to four times in 24 hours, instead of waiting six hours.
terms.equivalent: azure: live disk resize and performance tier change (close)

terms.definition: An io1/io2 feature that attaches one volume to up to 16 Nitro instances in the same AZ, which requires a cluster-aware file system to avoid corruption.
An EBS option (May 2025) that hydrates a volume created from a snapshot at a specified rate, giving a predictable time to full performance as a cheaper alternative to Fast Snapshot Restore.

A retention service that keeps deleted EBS snapshots, EBS-backed AMIs and, since 20 Nov 2025, EBS volumes for a rule-defined period so they can be restored after accidental deletion; rules can be locked.
terms.equivalent: azure: soft delete for disk snapshots and backups (close)

terms.definition: An incremental, Regional point-in-time backup of an EBS volume stored durably by AWS, which can be copied across Regions and accounts, archived, protected by Recycle Bin, or pre-warmed with Fast Snapshot Restore.

A WORM setting (November 2023) that stops snapshots being deleted for a set period, in governance mode (removable with permission) or compliance mode (not even by root after the cooling-off period), for ransomware protection.
terms.equivalent: azure: immutable vaults in Azure Backup (partial)

terms.definition: A logical group of EC2 instances spanning AZs that keeps capacity between minimum and maximum, replaces unhealthy instances, and scales according to policies using a launch template.

A way to reserve GPU or Trainium instances in co-located clusters for a fixed future window, paid upfront: 1-14 days or multiples of 7 days up to 182 days, starting up to 8 weeks ahead, with no cancellation, no placement groups, up to 64 instances per block and 256 across blocks, shareable within an organization (Feb 2026).
An EC2 feature (October 2025) that gives multi-account visibility into On-Demand, Spot and Capacity Reservation usage and utilization so teams can rightsize reservations.
terms.equivalent: azure: capacity reservation utilization in Azure portal (partial)

terms.definition: Fleet APIs that launch a mix of On-Demand and Spot capacity across instance types and AZs using allocation strategies and target capacity; EC2 Fleet can target Capacity Reservations, and AWS recommends Auto Scaling groups or EC2 Fleet over the legacy Spot Fleet API.
terms.equivalent: azure: VMSS flexible orchestration with Spot priority mix (partial)

terms.definition: Stopping an EBS-backed instance after saving its RAM to the encrypted root volume, so it resumes with in-memory state and preloaded applications, with no compute charges while stopped.
A managed pipeline service that builds, hardens, tests and distributes AMIs and container images on a schedule or trigger.
A VPC endpoint that provides IAM-authorized SSH and RDP to instances in private subnets with no public IP, bastion host or agent required.
Physically attached NVMe or HDD block storage on the host whose data is lost when the instance stops, hibernates, terminates or its hardware fails, suited to caches, buffers and replicated data.
A named hardware profile such as m8g.xlarge that encodes family, generation, processor and attributes, and size, and determines vCPU, memory, storage, network bandwidth and accelerators.
A versioned EC2 launch specification (AMI, instance type, network, IAM profile, metadata options, user data) used by RunInstances, Auto Scaling groups and EC2 Fleet.
terms.equivalent: azure: VM Scale Set model / template spec (partial)

terms.definition: An EC2 placement strategy: cluster packs instances for low latency in one AZ, partition separates groups across racks, spread places up to seven instances per AZ on distinct hardware, and precision time uses hardware with high-precision time sources.
terms.equivalent: azure: proximity placement group / availability set (partial)

terms.definition: EC2's automated health checks of the host (system), the guest OS and networking (instance) and attached EBS volumes; simplified automatic recovery moves supported instances to new hardware when the system check fails.
terms.equivalent: azure: VM Resource Health and VM auto-recovery (close)

terms.definition: A script or cloud-init directive (up to 16 KB) passed at launch that the instance runs at first boot by default, readable through the instance metadata service.
A stateful VPC gateway that lets IPv6 resources initiate outbound internet connections while blocking unsolicited inbound IPv6 connections.
A network device for HPC and ML instances that adds OS-bypass (libfabric/NCCL) communication over AWS's SRD protocol for tightly coupled MPI and distributed training or inference.
A static public IPv4 address allocated to an account that can be remapped between instances or network interfaces; like every public IPv4 address, it is billed hourly.
AWS's managed load balancing family: Application, Network, Gateway and Classic Load Balancers, which distribute traffic to registered targets across AZs with health checks.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Load Balancer / Application Gateway family (partial)

terms.definition: The SR-IOV enhanced networking interface on Nitro instances that provides high bandwidth and packets per second; ENA Express uses SRD to raise single-flow throughput and reduce tail latency, and since 2026 also works across AZs.
A virtual network card in a subnet that carries private and public IPs, security groups and a MAC address, and can be attached to or moved between instances.
terms.equivalent: azure: network interface (NIC) (close; an ENI can be hot-attached and moved between instances, while an Azure NIC is bound to a VM at creation)

terms.definition: How ELB picks a target: ALB target groups use round robin, least outstanding requests or weighted random (optionally with Automatic Target Weights anomaly mitigation, November 2023), while NLB hashes each flow's 5-tuple to a target.
terms.equivalent: azure: Load Balancer hash distribution and Application Gateway round robin (partial)

terms.definition: Binding a client to one target: ALB uses duration-based load balancer cookies or application-based cookies per target group, while NLB uses source-IP affinity.
A set of instance, IP, Lambda or ALB targets with a protocol, port and health check that listener rules route to; it can be weighted or shared across load balancers.
A Deny statement matching a request in any applicable policy; it overrides every Allow, wherever that Allow comes from.
A layer 3 load balancer that transparently distributes traffic over GENEVE (port 6081) to fleets of third-party virtual appliances, reached through Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in route tables.
terms.equivalent: azure: Gateway Load Balancer, which uses VXLAN (close)

terms.definition: A free VPC endpoint for S3 or DynamoDB, implemented as a prefix-list route in route tables, that keeps traffic on the AWS network but cannot be reached from on-premises or peered networks.
An IAM capability that uses automated reasoning to report external, internal and unused access, validate and custom-check policies, and generate least-privilege policies from CloudTrail activity.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra access reviews plus Defender for Cloud permissions management (partial)

terms.definition: A long-term credential pair for an IAM user or root user used to sign programmatic requests; best practice is to replace it with temporary credentials.

A named attribute of the request context that a policy Condition element compares using operators like StringEquals or ArnLike; global keys (aws:*, such as aws:SourceIp or aws:PrincipalTag) are available across services, while service-specific keys (such as s3:prefix) exist only for that service's actions.
A collection of IAM users in one account that share attached policies; it is not a principal, so it cannot be named in a resource-based policy or assumed.

An IAM entity that registers an external SAML 2.0 or OIDC issuer in an account, so its tokens can be exchanged for role credentials; claim checks are mandatory for shared providers such as GitHub Actions.
IAM data showing when principals last used each service and action, plus a downloadable credential report of users' password and key status, used to remove unused permissions and credentials.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra sign-in logs and access reviews (partial)

terms.definition: An account-level IAM feature that lets AWS principals call STS GetWebIdentityToken for a short-lived signed JWT, so they can authenticate to external services (including other clouds) without stored secrets.
terms.equivalent: azure: managed identity tokens presented to external relying parties (partial)

terms.definition: The IAM permission a principal needs to hand a role to an AWS service (for example when launching EC2 with an instance profile or creating a Lambda function); it is the main privilege-escalation path to control, usually scoped with iam:PassedToService.
terms.equivalent: azure: Managed Identity Operator role to assign identities (partial)

terms.definition: The algorithm AWS uses to decide each request: an explicit deny anywhere wins; RCPs, SCPs, permissions boundaries and session policies must all allow, because they are ceilings; within one account an allow in either an identity-based or a resource-based policy grants access, with exceptions for role trust and KMS key policies and for role-ARN vs role-session-ARN principals; cross-account requests need an allow on both sides.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure RBAC evaluation of role and deny assignments (partial)

terms.definition: A console and API tool that evaluates which actions a principal's policies (including permissions boundaries and SCP effects) would allow or deny, without making real requests.
terms.equivalent: azure: check access in Azure RBAC (partial)

terms.definition: A placeholder, such as ${aws:username} or ${aws:PrincipalTag/team}, that IAM replaces with request-context values at evaluation time, so one policy can scope access per principal.
terms.equivalent: azure: ABAC attribute references in conditions (partial)

terms.definition: The kinds of identity a policy can name: AWS accounts and root, IAM users, IAM roles, role sessions (arn:aws:sts::...:assumed-role/...), federated users, and AWS service principals such as lambda.amazonaws.com in trust policies; evaluation differs for a role ARN vs a role session ARN.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra security principals (user, group, service principal, managed identity) (partial)

terms.definition: An identity with permission policies and a trust policy but no long-term credentials, which trusted principals assume through AWS STS to receive temporary credentials.
terms.equivalent: azure: managed identity or service principal plus Azure RBAC role assignment (partial)

terms.definition: A feature that lets workloads outside AWS present X.509 certificates from a registered trust anchor (CA) to obtain temporary IAM role credentials instead of long-term access keys.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Arc-enabled server managed identity (partial)

terms.definition: An identity defined in one AWS account that holds long-term credentials (a console password and/or access keys) and that AWS now recommends only for cases federation and roles cannot cover.
A JSON permissions policy attached to an IAM user, group or role that states which actions that identity may perform on which resources, under which conditions.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure RBAC role definition plus assignment (partial)

terms.definition: The user and group store that IAM Identity Center authenticates against: its built-in Identity Center directory, Active Directory, or an external SAML 2.0 identity provider with SCIM provisioning.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra ID tenant or hybrid identity sync (partial)

terms.definition: An IAM Identity Center session (August 2025) that lets a trusted application keep acting for a signed-in workforce user, through trusted identity propagation, after the user goes offline, such as for long-running analytics or agent jobs.

A console role session that IAM Identity Center links to the workforce user's identity (renamed in May 2025), so console actions in supporting services carry the user context for trusted identity propagation.
The default denial of any request that no applicable policy explicitly allows, which an Allow added later can overcome.
terms.equivalent: azure: no role assignment grants the action (exact)

terms.definition: A policy embedded directly in one user, group or role that is deleted with that identity, used when a strict one-to-one relationship is needed.
A container that passes one IAM role to an EC2 instance, so software on the instance gets automatically rotated temporary credentials from the instance metadata service.
terms.equivalent: azure: system-assigned managed identity on a VM (close)

terms.definition: An AWS solution that starts and stops EC2 instances, Auto Scaling groups and RDS databases on tag-driven schedules across accounts, the standard way to cut non-production compute cost out of hours.
A PrivateLink-powered set of ENIs with private IPs in your subnets (billed per AZ-hour and per GB) that gives private, DNS-integrated access to AWS services or endpoint services.
A horizontally scaled, highly available VPC component that routes traffic between a VPC and the internet and performs one-to-one NAT for instances with public IPv4 addresses.
terms.equivalent: azure: implicit internet routing with public IP (partial)

terms.definition: An open-source AWS solution that deploys a configuration-driven, compliance-oriented multi-account baseline via CDK pipelines, often on top of Control Tower.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Landing Zones Terraform/Bicep modules (close)

terms.definition: The legacy, immutable Auto Scaling launch specification that supports no instance types released after 2022 and cannot be created at all by accounts opened on or after October 1, 2024.

The ELB billing and scaling unit measured on new connections, active connections, processed bytes and (ALB) rule evaluations; capacity unit reservation (November 2024) pre-provisions a minimum for ALB and NLB ahead of known surges.
A named, versioned set of CIDR blocks, customer- or AWS-managed (for example CloudFront origin-facing IPs), that can be referenced in security groups and route tables and shared via RAM.
The account that creates and pays for an organization; it controls policies and membership, is not restricted by SCPs or RCPs, and should therefore run no workloads.
terms.equivalent: azure: billing account owner plus tenant root management group (partial)

terms.definition: Any account in an organization other than the management account; it is subject to inherited organization policies and its usage rolls up to consolidated billing.

A managed network address translation service that lets resources in private subnets reach the internet or other networks without accepting inbound connections; zonal gateways live in one AZ, and private NAT gateways translate to private IPs.
A self-managed EC2 instance with source/destination check disabled that performs NAT, which is cheaper at low throughput but requires you to handle scaling, patching and failover.
A VPC tool that finds unintended network access paths matching defined scopes, such as internet-reachable databases, to verify segmentation requirements.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Virtual Network Manager verifier (partial)

terms.definition: A stateless, subnet-level firewall with numbered allow and deny rules evaluated in order, which needs explicit return-traffic rules for ephemeral ports.
terms.equivalent: azure: NSG on a subnet, which is stateful (partial)

terms.definition: AWS Network Firewall rule groups written as domain lists, standard 5-tuple rules or Suricata-compatible IPS rules, evaluated either in the default action order (pass, drop, reject, alert) or in strict order with a default action.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Firewall rule collections and IDPS signatures (partial)

terms.definition: A layer 4 load balancer for TCP, UDP, TLS and QUIC with ultra-low latency, a static IP per AZ, client IP preservation and optional TLS termination; it can front PrivateLink endpoint services.

A Network Manager tool that analyzes routes in transit gateway route tables between two attachments or IPs, in both directions, to find missing or blackhole routes; unlike Reachability Analyzer it does not evaluate security groups or NACLs.

A reservation of EC2 capacity for an instance type in a specific AZ, billed at On-Demand rates whether used or not, with no term commitment; it can be future-dated, shared, and (since 2025) made interruptible.
terms.equivalent: azure: on-demand capacity reservation (close; AWS adds future-dated and interruptible reservations and RAM sharing)

terms.definition: EC2 capacity paid per second or hour with no commitment, which gives maximum flexibility at the highest unit price and no capacity guarantee.
A container for accounts and nested OUs (up to five levels below the root) in an AWS organization, used to apply policies to groups of accounts.

An Organizations declarative policy that deploys and enforces AWS Backup plans (schedules, vaults, copy rules, resource selection by tag) across accounts, merging inherited settings from the root and OUs.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy deploying Azure Backup (partial)

terms.definition: A declarative policy type that enforces EC2 and VPC account attributes across an organization, such as VPC Block Public Access, Allowed AMIs, image and snapshot block public access, IMDS defaults and serial console access.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy built-ins for VM and network settings (partial)

terms.definition: An Organizations setting that lets a specific AWS service operate across all accounts (creating service-linked roles as needed) to provide organization-wide features.

The mechanism in which hosts learn the smallest MTU on a path from ICMP 'fragmentation needed' or 'packet too big' messages; it fails when security groups or NACLs block that ICMP, the classic packet-size mismatch.
An IAM Identity Center template of policies (AWS managed, customer managed, inline, optional permissions boundary) that is provisioned as an IAM role in each account where it is assigned.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure RBAC role assigned to an Entra group at subscription scope (partial)

terms.definition: A managed policy set on an IAM user or role as the maximum permissions its identity-based policies can grant; on its own it grants nothing.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure ABAC conditions constraining delegated role assignment (partial)

terms.definition: An Auto Scaling policy that forecasts load from historical cyclical patterns and provisions capacity ahead of demand, usually combined with target tracking.
A binary header that NLB can prepend to TCP connections to pass the original client IP and port (and PrivateLink endpoint ID) to targets when client IP preservation is off.
terms.equivalent: azure: Private Link Service TCP proxy v2 (close)

terms.definition: The hourly charge AWS applies since February 2024 to every public IPv4 address, in use or idle, including those on NAT gateways and load balancers; it is a primary network cost driver and a reason to adopt IPv6.

A NAT gateway mode (November 2025) that expands and contracts across Availability Zones automatically as workloads move, needs no public subnet, allows up to 32 IPs per AZ (vs 8) and can draw your own IPs through IPAM policies; it does not support private NAT, is not available in constrained AZs, and can take up to 60 minutes to expand into a new AZ, processing traffic cross-zone meanwhile.
A one- or three-year billing discount for a specific instance configuration; Standard RIs can be resold, Convertible RIs can be exchanged, and only zonal RIs also reserve capacity.

ENIs that VPC Resolver creates in your subnets: inbound endpoints accept DNS queries from on-premises or other networks, and outbound endpoints forward queries to external resolvers according to rules.
terms.equivalent: azure: DNS Private Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints (close; Azure endpoints live in dedicated delegated subnets and the resolver is one resource per VNet)

terms.definition: A VPC Resolver rule that forwards queries for a domain through an outbound endpoint to specified DNS servers; it is associated with VPCs and can be shared across accounts via RAM.
terms.equivalent: azure: DNS forwarding ruleset (close; an Azure ruleset groups rules and links to VNets, while AWS shares individual rules through RAM)

terms.definition: A JSON policy attached to a resource, such as an S3 bucket, KMS key or SQS queue, that names the principals (including other accounts) allowed to act on it, enabling cross-account access without role assumption.
terms.equivalent: azure: resource-scoped role assignment or SAS (partial)

terms.definition: An organization authorization policy (since November 2024) that caps the permissions any principal, including principals outside the organization, can have on resources of supported services in member accounts; it does not apply to service-linked roles, AWS managed KMS keys or management-account resources, and RCPFullAWSAccess is attached automatically when RCPs are enabled.
Using credentials from one assumed role to assume another role, which limits the resulting session to at most one hour regardless of the role's maximum session duration.
The resource-based policy on an IAM role that specifies which principals (accounts, services, federated identity providers) can assume it, and under which conditions.
terms.equivalent: azure: federated identity credential on an app registration or managed identity (partial)

terms.definition: A Route 53 extension record that points a name, including the zone apex, at AWS resources such as ELB, CloudFront, S3 websites or VPC endpoints, follows their IP changes automatically, and incurs no query charge for AWS targets.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure DNS alias record set (close)

terms.definition: A VPC Resolver feature that allows, alerts on or blocks outbound DNS queries using domain lists and managed threat lists, with Advanced rules that detect DNS tunneling and DGA domains.
DNSSEC signing of public hosted zones with a key-signing key backed by an asymmetric KMS key, plus DNSSEC validation of responses by VPC Resolver for queries from VPCs.

An internet-reachable anycast DNS resolver for authorized clients that resolves public and private hosted zones over Do53, DoT and DoH, with filtering, logging and Regional failover; its arrival is why Route 53 Resolver was renamed VPC Resolver, but the GA date is not yet confirmed from the Route 53 documentation history.
A Route 53 monitor of an endpoint, other health checks (calculated) or a CloudWatch alarm, whose status drives DNS failover and the removal of unhealthy records.
A Route 53 container of DNS records for one domain; public zones answer internet queries, and private zones answer only from associated VPCs (including VPCs in other accounts).
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure DNS zone / private DNS zone (close)

terms.definition: A shareable bundle of DNS configuration (private hosted zones, Resolver rules, DNS Firewall rule groups, interface endpoints) that can be applied to many VPCs and accounts at once.

Two separate features: public DNS query logs record queries Route 53 answers for public hosted zones and go to CloudWatch Logs, while VPC Resolver query logs record queries from VPCs and go to CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Firehose.
terms.equivalent: azure: DNS security policy logs and Azure DNS metrics (partial)

terms.definition: The rule Route 53 applies to choose answers for a record set: simple, weighted, latency-based, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, IP-based or multivalue answer, optionally combined with health checks.
A versioned Route 53 Traffic Flow document that combines routing policies, health checks and endpoints into a tree applied to one or more policy records, built in a visual editor or JSON.

The recursive DNS resolver available by default in every VPC at the VPC+2 address, which answers for VPC names, private hosted zones and public domains, and extends to hybrid DNS through Resolver endpoints and rules.

A one- or three-year commitment to a dollar-per-hour spend in exchange for discounts: Compute Savings Plans apply across EC2 families, Regions, Fargate and Lambda, while EC2 Instance Savings Plans give deeper discounts locked to a family in a Region.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure savings plan for compute (close)

terms.definition: A stateful, allow-only virtual firewall attached to network interfaces that filters traffic by protocol, port and source or destination (CIDR, prefix list or another security group).
terms.equivalent: azure: network security group on a NIC plus ASGs (partial; NSGs have allow and deny rules with priorities and default rules and attach to subnets or NICs, while security groups are allow-only, attach only to ENIs and can reference other groups)

terms.definition: How security groups keep state: most flows are tracked, flows allowed by all-open rules in both directions are untracked, and tracked flows expire after configurable idle timeouts; Nitro v6 cut the default established TCP idle timeout from 432,000 s to 350 s.

An organization authorization policy that sets the maximum permissions available to IAM users and roles (including member-account root) in the targeted accounts; it never grants, and it does not affect the management account or service-linked roles.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy deny effect or deny assignments (partial)

terms.definition: A predefined IAM role linked to a specific AWS service, which only that service can assume and whose permissions the service defines; SCPs and RCPs do not restrict it.
terms.equivalent: azure: first-party service principals for Azure resource providers (partial)

terms.definition: The AWS service for viewing default and applied quotas (per account, Region or resource), requesting increases, applying request templates across an organization, and alarming on usage before limits are hit.
An inline or managed policy passed when assuming a role or federating a user, which further restricts that single session's permissions to the intersection with the role's policies.
Key-value attributes passed when assuming a role or federating (often from IdP claims) that act as principal tags for that session and can optionally carry through role chaining.
terms.equivalent: azure: token claims used in ABAC conditions (partial)

terms.definition: A preview Shield capability (June 2025; multi-account support December 2025) that inventories network resources, finds configuration gaps against best practices and recommends WAF, Network Firewall and security group fixes; it has its own Organizations declarative policy type.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Network Security Perimeter recommendations in Defender for Cloud (partial)

terms.definition: AWS's DDoS experts that Shield Advanced subscribers (with a Business-tier or higher support plan) can engage around the clock to analyze and mitigate attacks, including proactive engagement on health-check alarms.

The AWS request-signing protocol in which the caller derives a signing key from its secret access key, date, Region and service and signs a canonical form of each request; SigV4a signs with an asymmetric key valid across Regions, as multi-Region access points require.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra ID bearer tokens or Shared Key signing (partial)

terms.definition: Serving different answers for the same name to internal and external clients, on AWS by pairing a public hosted zone with a private hosted zone of the same name associated with VPCs.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure DNS public zone plus private DNS zone of the same name (close)

terms.definition: Spare EC2 capacity at steep discounts that AWS can reclaim with a two-minute interruption notice, best for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads diversified across instance types and AZs.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Spot VMs, with 30-second eviction notice (close)

terms.definition: The STS API an authenticated AWS principal calls to obtain temporary credentials for a role it is trusted to assume, which is the standard mechanism for cross-account access.
The STS API that exchanges a SAML 2.0 assertion from a corporate identity provider for temporary role credentials, the basis of direct IAM SAML federation.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra ID SAML SSO to an enterprise app (partial)

terms.definition: The STS API that exchanges a JWT from a trusted OIDC identity provider (for example GitHub Actions, Entra ID or Cognito) for temporary role credentials, without any AWS credentials beforehand.

The STS API (November 2024) that the management or delegated administrator account calls to get a short, task-scoped privileged root session in a member account, limited to a task policy such as deleting root credentials or unlocking a misconfigured S3 bucket or SQS queue policy.

A per-customer identifier that a third party generates, keeps unique per customer and controls, passes in AssumeRole, and that the role's trust policy checks with sts:ExternalId to prevent the cross-account confused deputy; it protects because the customer cannot choose it, not because it is secret.
An immutable identifier, such as a username, that is set when a role is first assumed, persists through role chaining and is logged in CloudTrail to attribute actions to the original human.
An Organizations declarative policy that standardizes tag keys, capitalization and allowed values, and can prevent non-compliant tagging operations for specified resource types.

An Auto Scaling policy that adds or removes capacity to keep a metric, such as average CPU or ALB requests per target, at a target value; it is preferred over step scaling (alarm-threshold bands) and simple scaling (single adjustment with cooldown).
A VPC attachment setting that keeps both directions of a flow on the same AZ's network interface, so stateful inspection appliances see symmetric traffic.
A transit gateway attachment type that runs GRE tunnels with BGP to SD-WAN or virtual appliances over a VPC or Direct Connect transport attachment.
terms.equivalent: azure: Virtual WAN NVA in hub / BGP peering (partial)

terms.definition: A transit gateway construct that delivers multicast traffic between subnets of attached VPCs, with static sources or IGMPv2 group membership, for applications that need one-to-many delivery.
A transit gateway attachment (June 2025) that connects AWS Network Firewall directly to a transit gateway, so centralized inspection no longer needs a dedicated inspection VPC.
terms.equivalent: azure: secured virtual hub with Azure Firewall (close)

terms.definition: A transit gateway feature (22 Oct 2026) that translates addresses one-to-one between attachments, so networks with overlapping CIDRs can communicate without re-addressing or an appliance.
terms.equivalent: azure: Virtual WAN VPN NAT rules (partial)

terms.definition: An attachment that connects two transit gateways in the same or different Regions over the AWS backbone with static routes only, the hand-built mesh that Cloud WAN replaces with policy.

A transit gateway feature (GA 28 Jul 2026) that routes traffic by policy rules on packet attributes rather than destination prefix alone; it differs from the 2022 policy tables, which apply only to peering attachments.
terms.equivalent: azure: Virtual WAN routing intent and policies (partial)

terms.definition: A routing domain inside a transit gateway: each attachment is associated with one table that routes its traffic, and propagates its routes into any number of tables, which allows segmentation such as isolated VPCs with shared services.
terms.equivalent: azure: Virtual WAN hub route tables (close)

terms.definition: A legacy hub-and-spoke pattern in which VPN or SD-WAN appliances in a central VPC connect spoke VPCs and on-premises sites over IPsec tunnels; Transit Gateway replaced it, but it still appears in ANS-C01 scenarios.

An IAM Identity Center capability that carries a user's workforce identity through supporting applications and AWS services, so data access can be authorized and audited per user rather than per application role.
The AWS-side VPN and Direct Connect concentrator attached to a single VPC, which can propagate learned routes into that VPC's route tables.

An account- and Region-level setting (November 2024) that blocks traffic through internet gateways and egress-only internet gateways for VPCs and subnets, with exclusions, and can be enforced by declarative policy.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy denying public IPs (partial)

terms.definition: A VPC feature (November 2025) that monitors or enforces encryption in transit for traffic within and between VPCs in a Region, using Nitro hardware encryption or application TLS, with a monitor mode and an enforce mode.
A resource-based policy on a gateway or interface endpoint that limits which principals, actions and resources can be reached through that endpoint.

Metadata records of IP traffic to and from network interfaces, subnets, VPCs or transit gateways (addresses, ports, action, bytes and optional extended fields), delivered to CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Firehose; they are not packet captures.
A VPC feature for planning, allocating and monitoring IPv4, IPv6 and BYOIP address space across accounts and Regions with scopes, hierarchical pools and allocation rules.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Virtual Network Manager IPAM (close)

terms.definition: An IAM resource policy on a Lattice service network or service that authorizes SigV4-signed requests by principal, organization and request attributes, giving service-level authorization that PrivateLink does not provide.
A one-to-one, non-transitive private connection between two VPCs (same or different account or Region) with non-overlapping CIDRs; it has no bandwidth bottleneck and no edge-to-edge routing.
A configuration analysis tool that determines, without sending packets, whether a path between two resources is reachable and names the blocking component if not.
terms.equivalent: azure: Network Watcher connection troubleshoot / IP flow verify (partial)

terms.definition: VPC resource constructs (December 2024): a resource gateway is the entry point in the provider VPC, and a resource configuration describes a TCP resource (an IP, DNS name or RDS database) shared through RAM for consumers to reach via a Lattice service network or a PrivateLink resource endpoint.
terms.equivalent: azure: Private Link Service with direct connect (partial)

terms.definition: A VPC feature (March 2025) that peers over BGP with appliances inside a VPC and dynamically updates VPC and gateway route tables for routing fault tolerance.

A set of destination-to-target routes associated with subnets (or with gateways for ingress routing) that the VPC router uses with longest-prefix match; every table includes a non-removable local route.
Sharing subnets of a VPC owned by one account with other accounts in the same organization via RAM, so participants deploy resources into a centrally managed network.
A range of a VPC's addresses confined to one Availability Zone (with five addresses reserved); it is public if its route table sends traffic to an internet gateway, and private otherwise.
terms.equivalent: azure: VNet subnet, which is regional and zone-spanning (partial)

terms.definition: A feature that copies full packets from ENIs, filtered by rules and wrapped in VXLAN, to an NLB, GWLB endpoint or ENI target for deep packet inspection; it is not supported on Nitro v5 or v6 instances (for example M8g, M9g, C8i), so many current-generation instances cannot be mirror sources.
terms.equivalent: azure: virtual network TAP / Network Watcher packet capture (partial)

terms.term: AWS WAF Anti-DDoS managed rule group
terms.definition: An AWS WAF managed rule group (June 2025) that detects HTTP request floods within seconds and challenges or blocks suspect traffic, including resource-level protection for ALB; since 26 Mar 2026 it is the default HTTP-flood protection and supersedes Shield Advanced Layer 7 Auto Mitigation.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure WAF HTTP DDoS ruleset (close)

terms.definition: A paid WAF managed rule group with common and targeted protection levels that labels, verifies and limits bots; 2026 updates added Web Bot Auth verification of signed agent requests and an AI traffic analysis dashboard, relevant when AI agents call your sites.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure WAF bot protection ruleset (partial)

terms.definition: A WAF rule that counts requests per aggregation key (such as IP, forwarded IP, header or label) over a chosen window and blocks, challenges or counts keys that exceed a limit; the basic layer 7 throttling and flood control.

pairs.difference: Security groups are stateful, allow-only and attached to ENIs; NACLs are stateless, ordered allow/deny rules on subnets, so return traffic on ephemeral ports must be allowed explicitly.
A role has no long-term credentials and issues temporary STS credentials to whoever its trust policy allows; a user holds a permanent password and access keys tied to one identity.
Identity-based policies attach to principals and cannot name a Principal; resource-based policies attach to resources, name principals and can grant cross-account access without role assumption.

Both only cap permissions, but an SCP applies to every principal in the targeted accounts from the organization level, while a boundary applies to one user or role and is set by account administrators.
SCPs cap what your principals can do anywhere; RCPs cap what anyone, including external principals, can do to your resources, and only for supported services.

SCPs filter API authorization and miss new APIs unless written broadly; declarative policies enforce a configuration state in the service's control plane, govern service-linked roles and survive new features.
An explicit Deny overrides every Allow from any policy type; an implicit deny is just the absence of an Allow and disappears as soon as any applicable policy allows the action.

Gateway endpoints are free route-table entries for S3 and DynamoDB that on-premises clients cannot use; interface endpoints are billed per-AZ ENIs with private IPs and DNS, reachable over VPN, Direct Connect and peering.

Peering is a free-of-hourly-charge, non-transitive one-to-one link with no bandwidth bottleneck; Transit Gateway is a billed regional hub with route tables that gives transitive, segmentable any-to-any routing for thousands of attachments.

Transit Gateway is a regional router you mesh by hand with peering and static routes; Cloud WAN is a global network declared in one policy document, with segments propagated automatically across Regions.

PrivateLink exposes one service or resource per endpoint, one-way at layer 4; Lattice joins many services and resources into a service network with layer 7 routing and IAM auth policies, without per-consumer endpoints.
An internet gateway allows two-way internet traffic for resources with public IPs; a NAT gateway lets private resources initiate outbound connections only, hiding them behind its addresses.
A zonal NAT gateway lives in one AZ's public subnet, so high availability needs one per AZ and per-AZ routes; a regional NAT gateway spans AZs automatically and needs no public subnet.

VPN is encrypted IPsec over the internet, available in minutes but with variable latency; Direct Connect is a private physical circuit with consistent performance and weeks of lead time, unencrypted unless MACsec or VPN is layered on.

A private VIF reaches VPCs through a virtual private gateway (or a Direct Connect gateway to VGWs); a transit VIF reaches transit gateways through a Direct Connect gateway, giving one circuit access to many VPCs and Regions.

ALB terminates HTTP(S) and routes on content with layer 7 features such as authentication and JWT validation; NLB forwards TCP, UDP, TLS and QUIC at layer 4 with a static IP per AZ, client IP preservation and much lower latency.
NLB is an endpoint clients connect to; GWLB is a transparent bump-in-the-wire that wraps original packets in GENEVE to inspection appliances and returns them unchanged.

CloudFront caches and terminates HTTP(S), WebSocket and gRPC at the edge and now also offers Anycast static IPs; Global Accelerator does not cache and carries any TCP or UDP traffic over the AWS backbone to Regional endpoints with fast failover and client IP preservation, so non-HTTP protocols, not static IPs, are the deciding factor.

WAF filters layer 7 requests with rules you write or subscribe to, including the Anti-DDoS managed rule group that has been the default HTTP-flood protection since 26 Mar 2026; Shield Advanced is a DDoS subscription adding SRT support, cost protection and health-based detection, and its older Layer 7 Auto Mitigation continues only for existing customers.
Config records what a resource looks like over time and whether it is compliant; CloudTrail records which API call changed it, by whom and from where.
An alias works at the zone apex, resolves directly to AWS resource IPs and is free for AWS targets; a CNAME cannot sit at the apex and adds a resolution step.

Savings Plans commit to dollars per hour and apply flexibly across families (and, for Compute Savings Plans, Fargate and Lambda); RIs commit to an instance configuration, and only zonal RIs also reserve capacity.
A regional RI is a billing discount with no capacity guarantee; an ODCR guarantees capacity in one AZ at On-Demand price with no term, and the two can be combined.
Both are single-tenant, but only a Dedicated Host exposes sockets and cores and pins placement, which is what bring-your-own-license software counted per socket or core requires.

EBS volumes are network-attached, persist independently of the instance and can be snapshotted; instance store is physically local NVMe that is faster but lost on stop, hibernate, termination or host failure.

Cluster packs instances close together in one AZ for lowest latency at the price of correlated failure; spread puts each instance on distinct hardware (maximum seven per AZ) to minimize correlated failure.

Launch templates are versioned and support current instance types, mixed instances and new features; launch configurations are immutable legacy objects that new accounts cannot create at all since October 2024.

Identity Center centrally assigns permission sets across every account from one identity source; direct IAM SAML federation needs an identity provider and role mappings configured separately in each account.
A user pool authenticates end users and issues OIDC JWTs for your app; an identity pool exchanges such tokens for temporary AWS credentials to call AWS services directly.

EC2 Auto Scaling manages instance groups end to end (launch, health replacement, warm pools, instance refresh); Application Auto Scaling only adjusts a capacity number on other services such as ECS services, DynamoDB tables or Aurora replicas.

pairs.b: Predictive scaling policy on an Auto Scaling group
pairs.difference: A scaling plan spans an application's resources from one console plan; a predictive scaling policy lives on the group itself, which is where AWS now recommends configuring prediction.

EC2 Fleet launches a one-time or maintained mix of capacity from allocation strategies but has no health replacement integration with ELB or lifecycle hooks; an Auto Scaling group keeps a service healthy and scaled over time.
Reachability Analyzer checks the full configuration path, including security groups and NACLs, between two resources; Route Analyzer checks only transit gateway route tables between attachments.
Flow logs record connection metadata and work on every instance type; Traffic Mirroring copies full packets but is not supported on Nitro v5 or v6 sources.
Public query logs record what Route 53 answers for your public zones from the internet; Resolver query logs record what your VPC workloads ask, which is the one you need for egress investigations.

A tracked flow is remembered so return traffic is allowed and expires after an idle timeout; an untracked flow, allowed by all-open rules both ways, has no state to expire or to fill the tracking table.
A signed URL protects one object and changes its URL; signed cookies protect many objects, such as a whole site section, without changing URLs.
A cache policy decides what goes into the cache key and the TTLs; an origin request policy forwards extra headers, cookies or query strings to the origin without fragmenting the cache.

CloudFront Functions run lightweight JavaScript at every edge location on viewer events only; Lambda@Edge runs Node.js or Python at Regional edge caches with network access and origin events, at higher latency and cost.
A dedicated connection is your own physical port with many VIFs, LAGs and MACsec; a hosted connection is a partner-provisioned slice at a chosen speed with a single VIF.

A private NAT gateway hides an overlapping range behind a routable range for outbound-initiated traffic only; transit gateway 1:1 NAT maps addresses one-to-one between attachments, so either side can initiate.
A transit VPC is a customer-run hub of VPN appliances limited by instance throughput and tunnels; Transit Gateway is a managed regional router with route tables and no appliances to operate.
An external ID protects a role from a confused third-party account; aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount protect resources from a confused AWS service principal acting for another customer.

A resource policy that names the role ARN still lets boundaries and session policies limit the session; naming the session ARN grants that session directly, so implicit denies in those ceilings do not apply.
PassRole lets a principal give a role to a service that will use it; AssumeRole lets the principal itself take on the role's permissions.
An organization trail delivers log files to S3 for any query engine and stays open to all customers; CloudTrail Lake is a managed store and SQL engine that closed to new customers on 2026-05-31.
Service Catalog publishes any approved product for self-service provisioning; Account Factory is one specific Service Catalog product, maintained by Control Tower, that vends and enrolls accounts.
License-included pricing bundles Windows or SQL Server licenses per hour with no tracking; BYOL reuses licenses you own, often requiring Dedicated Hosts and License Manager to prove compliance.
Snapshot lock prevents deletion for a period, even by administrators in compliance mode; Recycle Bin lets deleted snapshots, AMIs and volumes be restored within a retention window.
Health reports events AWS is causing or scheduling for your resources; Trusted Advisor reports improvements you should make to your own configuration.
A rate-based rule enforces a fixed limit per key that you tune; the Anti-DDoS managed rule group learns a baseline and reacts to floods within seconds without a fixed threshold.
Deregistration delay drains in-flight requests at the load balancer; a lifecycle hook pauses the instance in Auto Scaling so your own scripts can finish work before it terminates.

- EBS volumes and snapshots are owned here. storage-data owns S3, EFS, FSx and AWS Backup.
- Cognito, Directory Service and Verified Permissions are owned in cloud/aws/identity.
- Firewall Manager and DNS Firewall are covered in networking. security-services links here.
- No ADR or cloud-compare pages are in these folders. Suggested ADRs: Transit Gateway vs Cloud WAN; centralized vs distributed egress; Identity Center vs direct federation; Control Tower vs LZA; NAT gateway model; overlapping-IP strategy.
- Exam codes: SAP-C02 is used for consistency with the other backlog sections. The repo's sap-c02.md retires 2026-11-16, and sap-c03.md (provisional) carries the same objectives, so remap SAP-C02:Dn to SAP-C03:Dn when the SAP-C03 guide publishes. The same applies to DVA-C02 and DVA-C03. ANS-C01 is catalogue-only in the repo (retires 2026-12-31). Its depth is kept for the architect track, but these pages can be scheduled after the SAA-C03, CLOUDOPS-A and SAP-C03 pages.
- Not on the ANS-C01 or SAP-C02 in-scope lists: Cloud WAN, VPC Lattice and Verified Access. Treat them as beyond-exam depth.
- The Azure equivalents are best mappings and should be checked by the Azure sections. The uncertain ones are Cobalt 100, Azure Local, Azure DNS security policy, VMSS standby pools, VNet encryption, and the Azure counterparts of Shield network security director and CloudFront Anycast static IPs.
